translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 202
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 202

sentences.zh: 卷第二百二

translations.literal: Volume Two Hundred Two
translations.idiomatic: Volume Two Hundred Two

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十八】起重光協洽，盡重光大荒落，凡十一年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 18] From Chongguang Xieqia through Chongguang Dahuangluo; eleven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 18] From Chongguang Xieqia through Chongguang Dahuangluo—eleven years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲子，上幸東都。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day jiazi: the emperor visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲申，以西突厥阿史那都支為左驍衛大將軍兼匐延都督，以安集五咄陸之眾。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiashen: Ashina Duzhi of the Western Turks was made General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and concurrently Governor of Fuyan, to settle and gather the people of the five Dulu tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the twenty-first day of the fourth month, Ashina Duzhi of the Western Turks was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and concurrently Governor of Fuyan, charged with pacifying and resettling the five Dulu tribes.

sentences.zh: 初，武元慶等既死，皇后奏以其姊子賀蘭敏之為士擭之嗣，襲爵周公，改姓武氏，累遷弘文館學士、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Wu Yuanqing and the others had died, the empress memorialized that her sister's son Helan Minzhi be made heir to Shi Yun, inherit the rank of Duke of Zhou, take the surname Wu, and be repeatedly promoted to Academician of the Hongwen Institute and Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wu Yuanqing and his kin had been put to death, the empress petitioned to have her sister's son Helan Minzhi succeed Shi Yun as heir, inherit the dukedom of Zhou, adopt the surname Wu, and rise through the ranks to Academician of the Hongwen Institute and Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 魏國夫人之死也，上見敏之，悲泣曰：「向吾出視朝猶無恙，退朝已不救，何倉卒如此！」

translations.literal: When the Lady of Wei died, the emperor saw Minzhi and wept, saying, "When I went out earlier to hold court she was still well; when I returned from court she could not be saved—how could it be so sudden!"
translations.idiomatic: After the Lady of Wei died, the emperor met Minzhi and wept, saying, "When I left court this morning she was still well; by the time I returned she could not be saved—how could it have happened so suddenly!"

sentences.zh: 敏之號哭不對。

translations.literal: Minzhi wailed loudly and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhi wailed but made no answer.

sentences.zh: -{后}-聞之，曰：「此兒疑我！」

translations.literal: The empress heard of it and said, "This boy suspects me!"
translations.idiomatic: When the empress heard of this, she said, "This boy suspects me!"

sentences.zh: 由是惡之。

translations.literal: From this she came to hate him.
translations.idiomatic: From that time she hated him.

sentences.zh: 敏之貌美，蒸於太原王妃；

translations.literal: Minzhi was handsome in appearance and had an illicit affair with the Princess of Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Minzhi was strikingly handsome and carried on an illicit affair with the Princess of Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 及居妃喪，釋衰絰，奏妓。

translations.literal: when he was in mourning for the princess, he cast off his hemp mourning garments and had singing girls perform.
translations.idiomatic: while in mourning for her, he cast off his mourning garments and had entertainers perform.

sentences.zh: 司衛少卿楊思儉女，有殊色，上及-{后}-自選以為太子妃，昏有日矣，敏之逼而淫之。

translations.literal: The daughter of Vice Minister of the Palace Guards Yang Sijian was of exceptional beauty; the emperor and empress had personally chosen her to be the crown prince's consort, and the wedding day was near, when Minzhi forced and violated her.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Vice Minister of the Palace Guards Yang Sijian was exceptionally beautiful; the emperor and empress had personally selected her as the crown prince's consort, and the wedding was imminent, when Minzhi forced himself upon her.

sentences.zh: -{后}-於是表言敏之前後罪惡，請加竄逐。

translations.literal: The empress thereupon memorialized on Minzhi's successive crimes and asked that he be banished.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then submitted a memorial detailing Minzhi's crimes and requesting that he be exiled.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，敕流雷州，復其本姓。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day bingzi: an edict banished him to Leizhou and restored his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the twenty-sixth day, an edict exiled him to Leizhou and restored his original surname.

sentences.zh: 至韶州，以馬韁絞死。

translations.literal: When he reached Shaozhou, he was strangled to death with a horse rein.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaozhou he was strangled with a horse rein.

sentences.zh: 朝士坐與敏之交遊，流嶺南者甚眾。

translations.literal: Court officials who were implicated for associating with Minzhi and banished to Lingnan were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials who had associated with Minzhi were implicated and exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙未朔，高侃破高麗餘眾於安市城。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day yimao: Gao Kan defeated the remaining Goguryeo forces at Anshi City.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, Gao Kan defeated the remaining Goguryeo troops at Anshi City.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申，潞州刺史徐王元禮薨。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day bingshen: Xu Wang Yuanli, governor of Luzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the fifteenth day, Prince Xu Yuanli, governor of Luzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，甲午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, first day jiawu: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day of the eleventh month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 車駕自東都幸許、汝；

translations.literal: The imperial carriage proceeded from the Eastern Capital to Xu and Ru;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor traveled from the Eastern Capital to Xu and Ru;

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸酉，校獵於葉縣；

translations.literal: twelfth month, day guiyou: held a hunting review at Ye County;
translations.idiomatic: in the twelfth month, on the tenth day, conducted a hunting expedition at Ye County;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，還東都。

translations.literal: day bingxu: returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-third day he returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，以太子右衛副率梁積壽為姚州道行軍總管，將兵討叛蠻。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day xinchou: Liang Jishou, Deputy Commander of the Crown Prince's Right Guard, was made Commander-in-Chief on campaign for the Yaozhou circuit, leading troops to attack rebellious barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the eighteenth day of the first month, Liang Jishou, Deputy Commander of the Crown Prince's Right Guard, was appointed campaign commander for the Yaozhou circuit and led troops against rebellious tribes.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，昆明蠻十四姓二萬三千戶內附，置殷、敦、總三州。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: the Kunming barbarians of fourteen clans, twenty-three thousand households, submitted; the three prefectures of Yin, Dun, and Zong were established.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day, twenty-three thousand households of fourteen Kunming clans submitted, and the prefectures of Yin, Dun, and Zong were established.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚午，徙吐谷渾於鄯州浩亹水南。

translations.literal: Second month, day gengwu: the Tuyuhun were moved south of the Hao River in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the seventh day, the Tuyuhun were relocated to the south bank of the Hao River in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾畏吐蕃之強，不安其居，又鄯州地狹，尋徙靈州，以其部落置安樂州，以可汗諾曷缽為刺史。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun feared the strength of the Tibetans and were uneasy in their dwelling; moreover Shanzhou's territory was narrow, and soon they were moved to Lingzhou, their tribes being placed in Anle Prefecture, with the qaghan Nuohebo made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun feared Tibetan power and could not settle peacefully; Shan Prefecture's land was also too cramped, so they were soon moved to Lingzhou, their tribes organized as Anle Prefecture, with Qaghan Nuohebo appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾故地皆入於吐蕃。

translations.literal: The former Tuyuhun lands all fell to the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: All the former Tuyuhun territories passed into Tibetan hands.

sentences.zh: 己卯，侍中永安郡公-{姜}-恪薨。

translations.literal: Day jimao: Jiang Ke, Duke of Yong'an and Palace Attendant, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day, Jiang Ke, Duke of Yong'an and Palace Attendant, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚午，上幸合璧宮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengwu: the emperor visited the Hebi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the seventh day of the fourth month, the emperor visited Hebi Palace.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣其大臣仲琮入貢，上問以吐蕃風俗，對曰：「吐蕃地薄氣寒，風俗樸魯；

translations.literal: Tibet sent its minister Zhongqiong to offer tribute; the emperor asked about Tibetan customs, and he replied, "Tibet's land is poor and its air cold; its customs are plain and rustic;
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent its minister Zhongqiong with tribute; when the emperor asked about Tibetan customs, he replied, "Tibet's soil is thin and its climate cold; its people are plain and unrefined;

sentences.zh: 然法令嚴整，上下一心，議事常自下而起，因人所利而行之，斯所以能持久也。」

translations.literal: yet its laws and orders are strict and orderly, superiors and subordinates of one mind; deliberations usually begin from below and proceed according to what benefits the people—this is why it can endure."
translations.idiomatic: yet its laws are strict and its people united; deliberations usually rise from the ranks and follow what benefits the people—that is how it endures."

sentences.zh: 上詰以吞滅吐谷渾、敗薛仁貴、寇逼涼州事，對曰：「臣受命貢獻而已，軍旅之事，非所聞也。」

translations.literal: The emperor questioned him about swallowing up the Tuyuhun, defeating Xue Rengui, and raiding toward Liangzhou; he replied, "Your servant was charged only to present tribute; military affairs are not what I have heard of."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him about the conquest of the Tuyuhun, the defeat of Xue Rengui, and raids toward Liangzhou; he replied, "I was charged only to present tribute; I have heard nothing of military affairs."

sentences.zh: 上厚賜而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor richly rewarded him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him generous gifts and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 癸未，遣都水使者黃仁素使於吐蕃。

translations.literal: Day guiwei: Commissioner of the Directorate of Waterways Huang Rensu was sent as envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day, Huang Rensu, Commissioner of the Directorate of Waterways, was dispatched as envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬午，特進高陽郡公許敬宗卒。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day renwu: Xu Jingzong, Duke of Gaoyang and Special Advancement, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the fourth day of the eighth month, Xu Jingzong, Duke of Gaoyang and Special Advancement, died.

sentences.zh: 太常博士袁思古議：「敬宗棄長子於荒徼，嫁少女於夷貊。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Yuan Sigu proposed: "Jingzong abandoned his eldest son in the remote frontier and married his young daughter to barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Sigu, erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, proposed: "Jingzong abandoned his eldest son to the frontier wastes and married his young daughter to barbarians.

sentences.zh: 按《謚法》，『名與實爽曰繆，』請謚為繆。」

translations.literal: According to the Posthumous Title Canon, 'when name and reality diverge it is called Miu (False),'—I ask that the posthumous title be Miu."
translations.idiomatic: According to the Posthumous Title Canon, 'when name and reality diverge, the title is Miu (False).' I request the posthumous title Miu."

sentences.zh: 敬宗孫太子舍人彥伯訟思古與許氏有怨，請改謚。

translations.literal: Jingzong's grandson Yanbo, Crown Prince Household Attendant, sued, saying Sigu bore a grudge against the Xu family and asked that the posthumous title be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong's grandson Yanbo, Attendant of the Crown Prince's Household, protested that Sigu bore a grudge against the Xu family and asked that the title be changed.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王福畤議，以為：「謚者得失一朝，榮辱千載。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Wang Fuchou proposed, holding that: "A posthumous title records gain and loss in a single morning, honor and shame for a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchou, another erudite of the court, argued: "A posthumous title fixes a man's worth in a moment and his reputation for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 若嫌隙有實，當據法推繩；

translations.literal: If private enmity has substance, one should apply the law and pursue it;
translations.idiomatic: If the grievance is genuine, let the law be applied;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，義不可奪。」

translations.literal: if not so, on principle it cannot be taken away."
translations.idiomatic: if not, the title must stand on principle."

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書戴至德謂福畤曰：「高陽公任遇如是，保以謚之為繆？」

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Dai Zhide said to Fuchou, "The Duke of Gaoyang received favor such as this—how can you guarantee giving him the posthumous title Miu?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Dai Zhide said to Fuchou, "The Duke of Gaoyang enjoyed such favor at court—how can you justify giving him the title Miu?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔晉司空何曾既忠且孝，徒以日食萬錢，秦秀謚之曰『繆』。

translations.literal: He replied, "Formerly Jin's Minister of Works He Zeng was both loyal and filial, yet solely because he spent ten thousand cash a day, Qin Xiu gave him the posthumous title 'Miu.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In Jin times He Zeng, Minister of Works, was loyal and filial, yet Qin Xiu gave him the title Miu solely because he spent ten thousand cash a day on food.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗忠孝不逮於曾，而飲食男女之累過之，謚之曰『繆』，無負許氏矣。」

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong did not reach Zeng in loyalty and filial piety, yet in the burdens of food, drink, and women he surpassed him—giving him the posthumous title 'Miu' does not wrong the Xu family."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong fell short of Zeng in loyalty and filial piety, yet exceeded him in indulgence in food, drink, and women—to title him Miu does the Xu family no wrong."

sentences.zh: 詔集五品已上更議，禮部尚書陽思敬議：「按《謚法》，既過能改曰恭。

translations.literal: An edict gathered officials of the fifth rank and above for further deliberation; Minister of Rites Yang Sijing proposed: "According to the Posthumous Title Canon, 'having faults yet able to reform is called Gong (Respectful).
translations.idiomatic: An edict called officials of the fifth rank and above to deliberate again; Minister of Rites Yang Sijing proposed: "According to the canon, 'having faults yet able to reform' yields the title Gong (Respectful).

sentences.zh: 請謚曰恭。」

translations.literal: I ask that the posthumous title be Gong."
translations.idiomatic: I request the title Gong."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嘗奏流其子昂於嶺南，又以女嫁蠻酋馮盎之子，多納其貨，故思古議及之。

translations.literal: Jingzong had once memorialized to banish his son Ang to Lingnan, and also married a daughter to the son of the barbarian chieftain Feng Ang, taking much of his goods—hence Sigu's proposal touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong had once had his son Ang exiled to Lingnan and had married a daughter to the son of the barbarian chieftain Feng Ang, accepting large bride-price payments—hence Sigu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 福畤，勃之父也。

translations.literal: Fuchou was the father of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchou was the father of Wang Bo.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸卯，徙沛王賢為雍王。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day guimao: Prince of Pei Xian was moved to Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the fourth day, Prince Pei Xian was redesignated Prince Yong.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己未，詔太子監國。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiwei: an edict ordered the crown prince to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the twenty-second day of the tenth month, an edict ordered the crown prince to govern in the emperor's absence.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，車駕發東都。

translations.literal: Day renxu: the imperial carriage departed the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day the emperor departed the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day wuzi: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，車駕至京師。

translations.literal: Day jiachen: the imperial carriage reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day the emperor reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月，高侃與高麗餘眾戰於白水山，破之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Gao Kan fought the remaining Goguryeo forces at Baishui Mountain and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Gao Kan fought the remaining Goguryeo forces at Baishui Mountain and routed them.

sentences.zh: 新羅遣兵救高麗，侃擊破之。

translations.literal: Silla sent troops to rescue Goguryeo; Kan struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Silla sent troops to aid Goguryeo; Kan defeated them as well.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以左庶子劉仁軌同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Day guimao: Left Junior Mentor Liu Ren'gui was made of the same rank as the Three Offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day, Liu Ren'gui, Left Junior Mentor, was appointed Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 太子罕接宮臣，典膳丞全椒邢文偉輒減所供膳，並上書諫太子。

translations.literal: The crown prince rarely received palace officials; Palace Provisioner Xing Wenwei of Quanjiao repeatedly reduced the meals supplied and also submitted a memorial admonishing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince rarely met with his palace staff; Xing Wenwei of Quanjiao, Director of Palace Provisions, repeatedly cut back his meals and submitted a memorial admonishing him.

sentences.zh: 太子復書，謝以多疾及入侍少暇，嘉納其意。

translations.literal: The crown prince wrote in reply, apologizing on grounds of many illnesses and little leisure because of attendance on the emperor, and commended his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wrote back, citing frequent illness and little leisure from attending the emperor, and thanked him for the advice.

sentences.zh: 頃之，右史缺，上曰：「邢文偉事吾子，能撤膳進諫，此直士也。」

translations.literal: Before long the Right Historian post was vacant; the emperor said, "Xing Wenwei serves my son, able to cut meals and offer remonstrance—this is an upright man."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the post of Right Historian fell vacant; the emperor said, "Xing Wenwei serves my son, yet dared to cut his provisions and remonstrate—he is an upright man."

sentences.zh: 擢為右史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Historian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Historian.

sentences.zh: 太子因宴集，命宮臣擲倒，次至左奉裕率王及善，及善曰：「擲倒自有伶官，臣若奉令，恐非所以羽翼殿下也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince at a banquet gathering ordered palace officials to perform tumbling; when it came to Left Director of Palace Attendants Wang Jishan, Jishan said, "Tumbling has its own entertainers; if your servant obeyed the order, I fear it would not be the way to support Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the crown prince ordered his attendants to perform acrobatic tumbling; when it came to Wang Jishan, Director of the Left Palace Attendants, he said, "Acrobats have their own performers; if I obeyed, I fear I would not be supporting Your Highness as I should."

sentences.zh: 太子謝之。

translations.literal: The crown prince apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince apologized.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，賜及善縑百匹，尋遷左千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and bestowed on Jishan one hundred bolts of silk, and soon promoted him to General of the Left Palace Interior Service.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he rewarded Jishan with one hundred bolts of silk and soon promoted him to General of the Left Palace Interior Service.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙辰，絳州刺史鄭惠王元懿薨。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day bingchen: Zheng Hui Wang Yuanyi, governor of Jiangzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the twenty-sixth day of the first month, Prince Zheng Hui Yuanyi, governor of Jiang Prefecture, died.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙申，詔劉仁軌等改修國史，以許敬宗等所記多不實故也。

translations.literal: Third month, day bingshen: an edict ordered Liu Ren'gui and others to revise the national history, because what Xu Jingzong and others had recorded was largely untrue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the sixteenth day, an edict ordered Liu Ren'gui and others to revise the national history, because Xu Jingzong's records were largely unreliable.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙子，車駕幸九成宮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingzi: the imperial carriage visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 閏五月，燕山道總管、右領軍大將軍李謹行大破高麗叛者於瓠蘆河之西，俘獲數千人，餘眾皆奔新羅。

translations.literal: Intercalary fifth month: Li Jinxing, Commander of the Yanshan circuit and General-in-Chief of the Right Palace Guards, greatly defeated Goguryeo rebels west of the Hulu River, capturing several thousand; the remaining forces all fled to Silla.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month, Li Jinxing, commander of the Yanshan circuit and General-in-Chief of the Right Palace Guards, routed Goguryeo rebels west of the Hulu River, taking several thousand prisoners; the rest fled to Silla.

sentences.zh: 時謹行妻劉氏留伐奴城，高麗引靺鞨攻之，劉氏擐甲帥眾守城，久之，虜退。

translations.literal: At that time Jinxing's wife Lady Liu remained at Fanu City; Goguryeo led Mohe to attack it; Lady Liu donned armor and led the troops in defending the city; after a long time the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxing's wife Lady Liu had remained at Fanu City when Goguryeo led Mohe forces against it; she donned armor, led the defense, and after a long siege the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其功，封燕國夫人。

translations.literal: The emperor commended her achievement and enfeoffed her as Lady of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised her achievement and enfeoffed her as Lady of Yan.

sentences.zh: 謹行，靺鞨人突地稽之子也，武力絕人，為眾夷所憚。

translations.literal: Jinxing was the son of the Mohe Tudiji, of surpassing martial strength, feared by all the barbarian peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxing was the son of the Mohe leader Tudiji, possessed of extraordinary strength, and feared among all the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛巳，婺州大水，溺死者五千人。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day xinsi: Wu Prefecture suffered great flooding; five thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the third day of the seventh month, Wu Prefecture suffered catastrophic flooding; five thousand people drowned.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛丑，上以瘧疾，令太子於延福殿受諸司啟事。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day xinchou: because of malarial illness the emperor ordered the crown prince to receive reports from all offices at Yanfu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the twenty-third day, the emperor, suffering from malaria, ordered the crown prince to receive memorials from all offices at Yanfu Hall.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬午，中書令閻立本薨。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day renwu: Yan Liben, Palace Attendant of the Secretariat, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the fourth day of the tenth month, Yan Liben, Grand Secretary of the Secretariat, died.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: Day yisi: the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙午，弓月、疏勒二王來降。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day bingwu: the kings of Gongyue and Shule came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the twenty-eighth day, the kings of Gongyue and Shule came to submit.

sentences.zh: 西突厥興昔亡可汗之世，諸部離散，弓月及阿悉吉皆叛。

translations.literal: In the time of the Western Turks' Qaghan Xingxianwang, the tribes scattered; Gongyue and Ashixi both rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Western Turk qaghan Xingxianwang, the tribes had scattered; Gongyue and Ashixi both rebelled.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方之西討也，擒阿悉吉以歸。

translations.literal: When Su Dingfang campaigned west, he captured Ashixi and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: On Su Dingfang's western campaign he captured Ashixi and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 弓月南結吐蕃，北招咽面，共攻疏勒，降之。

translations.literal: Gongyue allied with Tibet in the south and recruited Yanmian in the north, jointly attacking Shule and reducing it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyue allied with Tibet to the south and recruited Yanmian to the north, jointly attacking and subduing Shule.

sentences.zh: 上遣鴻臚卿蕭嗣業發兵討之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister of Ceremonial Xiao Siye to raise troops and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xiao Siye, Minister of Ceremonial, to raise troops against them.

sentences.zh: 嗣業兵未至，弓月懼，與疏勒皆入朝；

translations.literal: Before Siye's troops arrived, Gongyue grew afraid; he and Shule both entered court;
translations.idiomatic: Before Siye's army arrived, Gongyue grew afraid; he and the king of Shule both came to court;

sentences.zh: 上赦其罪，遣歸國。

translations.literal: the emperor pardoned their crimes and sent them back to their states.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor pardoned them and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬午，以左庶子、同中書門下三品劉仁軌為雞林道大總管，衛尉卿李弼、右領軍大將軍李謹行副之，發兵討新羅。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day renwu: Liu Ren'gui, Left Junior Mentor and of the same rank as the Three Offices, was made Grand Commander of the Jilin circuit; Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Li Bi and General-in-Chief of the Right Palace Guards Li Jinxing were his deputies, raising troops to attack Silla.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the fourth day of the first month, Liu Ren'gui, Left Junior Mentor and Grand Counselor, was appointed supreme commander of the Jilin circuit, with Li Bi, Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia, and Li Jinxing, General-in-Chief of the Right Palace Guards, as his deputies, to lead an expedition against Silla.

sentences.zh: 時新羅王法敏既納高麗叛眾，又據百濟故地，使人守之。

translations.literal: At that time the Silla king Fammin had both received Goguryeo rebels and occupied the former Baekje lands, sending men to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: The Silla king Fammin had sheltered Goguryeo rebels and occupied former Baekje territory, posting garrisons to hold it.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，詔削法敏官爵；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered Fammin's offices and titles stripped;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and stripped Fammin of his rank and titles;

sentences.zh: 其弟右驍衛員外大將軍、臨海郡公仁問在京師，立以為新羅王，使歸國。

translations.literal: his younger brother Renwen, Right Valiant Cavalry Guard Acting General-in-Chief and Duke of Linhai, was in the capital—he was established as king of Silla and sent to return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Renwen, Acting General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard and Duke of Linhai, who was in the capital, was installed as king of Silla and sent home.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Third month, first day xinhai: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭敏之既得罪，皇后奏召武元爽之子承嗣於嶺南，襲爵周公，拜尚衣奉御；

translations.literal: After Helan Minzhi had been punished, the empress memorialized to summon Wu Yuanshuang's son Chengsi from Lingnan, inherit the rank of Duke of Zhou, and appoint him Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe;
translations.idiomatic: After Helan Minzhi's downfall, the empress petitioned to recall Wu Yuanshuang's son Chengsi from Lingnan, have him inherit the dukedom of Zhou, and appoint him Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛卯，遷宗正卿。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinmao: he was moved to Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the twelfth day of the fourth month, he was promoted to Minister of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬辰，追尊宣簡公為宣皇帝，妣張氏為宣莊皇后；

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day renchen: posthumously honored Duke Xuanjian as Emperor Xuan, his mother Lady Zhang as Empress Xuanzhuang;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the third day of the eighth month, Duke Xuanjian was posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan and his mother Lady Zhang as Empress Xuanzhuang;

sentences.zh: 懿王為光皇帝，妣賈氏為光懿皇后；

translations.literal: Prince Yi as Emperor Guang, his mother Lady Jia as Empress Guangyi;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi as Emperor Guang and his mother Lady Jia as Empress Guangyi;

sentences.zh: 太武皇帝為神堯皇帝，太穆皇后為太穆神皇后；

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu as Emperor Shenyao, Empress Taimu as Divine Empress Taimu;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu as Emperor Shenyao and Empress Taimu as Divine Empress Taimu;

sentences.zh: 文皇帝為太宗文武聖皇帝，文德皇后為文德聖皇后。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen as Emperor Taizong the Civil and Martial Sage, Empress Wende as Sage Empress Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong as Emperor Taizong the Civil and Martial Sage, and Empress Wende as Sage Empress Wende.

sentences.zh: 皇帝稱天皇，皇后稱天-{后}-，以避先帝、先-{后}-之稱。

translations.literal: The emperor took the title Heavenly Emperor, the empress the title Heavenly Empress, to avoid the titles of the late emperor and late empress.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning emperor took the title Heavenly Emperor and the empress the title Heavenly Empress, so as not to share titles with the deceased emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 改元，赦天下。

translations.literal: The era name was changed and amnesty was granted to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，敕：「文武官三品以上服紫，金玉帶；

translations.literal: Day wuxu: an edict stated, "Civil and military officials of the third rank and above shall wear purple with gold and jade belts;
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day an edict declared: "Civil and military officials of the third rank and above shall wear purple robes with gold and jade belts;

sentences.zh: 四品服深緋，金帶；

translations.literal: fourth rank deep scarlet, gold belt;
translations.idiomatic: fourth rank deep scarlet with gold belts;

sentences.zh: 五品服淺緋，金帶；

translations.literal: fifth rank light scarlet, gold belt;
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank light scarlet with gold belts;

sentences.zh: 六品服深綠，七品服淺綠，並銀帶；

translations.literal: sixth rank deep green, seventh rank light green, all with silver belts;
translations.idiomatic: sixth rank deep green and seventh rank light green, all with silver belts;

sentences.zh: 八品服深青，九品服淺青，並金俞石帶；

translations.literal: eighth rank deep blue-green, ninth rank light blue-green, all with gold clasp and stone belt plaques;
translations.idiomatic: eighth rank deep blue-green and ninth rank light blue-green, all with ornamented metal and stone belts;

sentences.zh: 庶人服黃，銅鐵帶。

translations.literal: commoners wear yellow, copper and iron belts.
translations.idiomatic: commoners were to wear yellow with copper or iron belts.

sentences.zh: 自非庶人，不聽服黃。」

translations.literal: Apart from commoners, none were permitted to wear yellow."
translations.idiomatic: No one but commoners was permitted to wear yellow."

sentences.zh: 九月，癸丑，詔追復長孫晟、長孫無忌官爵，以無忌曾孫翼襲爵趙公，聽無忌喪歸，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day guichou: an edict restored the offices and titles of Zhangsun Sheng and Zhangsun Wuji; Wuji's great-grandson Yi inherited the rank of Duke of Zhao; Wuji's funeral was permitted to return, with burial attendant at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the twenty-third day, an edict restored the offices and titles of Zhangsun Sheng and Zhangsun Wuji, had Wuji's great-grandson Yi inherit the dukedom of Zhao, permitted Wuji's remains to be returned for burial, and allowed interment beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上御翔鸞閣，觀大□甫。

translations.literal: Day jiayin: the emperor ascended Xiangluan Pavilion to view the grand communal feast.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day the emperor went to Xiangluan Pavilion to watch the grand public feast.

sentences.zh: 分音樂為東西朋，使雍王賢主東朋，周王顯主西朋，角勝為樂。

translations.literal: Music was divided into eastern and western teams; Prince Yong Xian headed the eastern team and Prince Zhou Xian the western, competing for victory as entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: The musicians were divided into eastern and western sides; Prince Yong Xian led the east and Prince Zhou Xian the west, competing for victory as sport.

sentences.zh: 郝處俊諫曰：「二王春秋尚少，志趣未定，當推梨讓棗，相親如一。

translations.literal: Hao Chujun remonstrated, saying, "The two princes are still young in years and their inclinations are unsettled; they ought to yield pears and jujubes to one another and be as close as one.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Chujun remonstrated: "The two princes are still young and their characters not yet fixed; they ought to yield to one another like the boys of Liang and live in mutual affection.

sentences.zh: 今分二朋，遞相誇競，俳優小人，言辭無度，恐其交爭勝負，譏誚失禮，非所以崇禮義，勸敦睦也。」

translations.literal: Now, dividing them into two teams and having them boast and compete in turn, with actors and petty men speaking without measure—I fear they will dispute over victory and defeat, mock and lose propriety; this is not the way to exalt ritual and righteousness and encourage harmony."
translations.idiomatic: To divide them into rival camps and set them boasting against each other, with actors and low fellows speaking without restraint, risks quarrels over winning and losing, mockery, and breaches of decorum—it is no way to uphold ritual or foster brotherly harmony."

sentences.zh: 上瞿然曰：「卿遠識，非眾人所及也。」

translations.literal: The emperor started and said, "Your far-sightedness is not what the multitude can match."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said, "Your foresight is beyond what most men can match."

sentences.zh: 遽止之。

translations.literal: He immediately stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped the contest at once.

sentences.zh: 是日，衛尉卿李弼暴卒於宴所，為之廢□甫一日。

translations.literal: That day Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Li Bi died suddenly at the banquet place; for this the grand feast was suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Li Bi, Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia, died suddenly at the banquet; the grand feast was canceled for a day in mourning.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丙午朔，車駕發京師；

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, first day bingwu: the imperial carriage departed the capital;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day of the eleventh month, the emperor left the capital;

sentences.zh: 己酉，校獵華山之曲武原；

translations.literal: day jiyou: conducted a hunting review at Quwuyuan on Mount Hua;
translations.idiomatic: on the fourth day he hunted at Quwuyuan on Mount Hua;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，至東都。

translations.literal: day wuchen: reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-third day he reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 箕州錄事參軍張君澈等誣告刺史蔣王惲及其子汝南郡王煒謀反，敕通事舍人薛思貞馳傳往按之。

translations.literal: Zhang Junche, Records Officer of Ji Prefecture, and others falsely accused the governor Prince of Jiang Yun and his son Wei, Duke of Runan, of plotting rebellion; an edict ordered Imperial Transmission Attendant Xue Sizhen to ride post-haste to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Junche, records officer of Ji Prefecture, and others falsely accused Prince Jiang Yun, governor of Ji, and his son Wei, Duke of Runan, of treason; the emperor ordered Xue Sizhen, Attendant of Imperial Transmission, to investigate by urgent dispatch.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸未，惲惶懼，自縊死。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day guiwei: Yun, fearful and alarmed, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the tenth day, Yun, in terror, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 上知其非罪，深痛惜之，斬君澈等四人。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he was not guilty and deeply grieved for him; he beheaded Junche and three others.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yun innocent, the emperor grieved deeply and executed Junche and three accomplices.

sentences.zh: 戊子，于闐王伏闍雄來朝。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: the king of Khotan Fuzhanxiong came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day the king of Khotan, Fuzhanxiong, came to court.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，波斯王卑路斯來朝。

translations.literal: Day xinmao: the king of Persia Pilusi came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day the king of Persia, Pilusi, came to court.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，天-{后}-上表，以為：「國家聖緒，出自玄元皇帝，請令王公以下皆習《老子》，每歲明經，准《孝經》、《論語》策試。」

translations.literal: Day renyin: the Heavenly Empress submitted a memorial, holding that: "The sacred succession of the state derives from the Mysterious Primeval Emperor; I ask that nobles and officials down to the lowest all study the Laozi, and that each year in the Mingjing examination it be tested by policy questions on a par with the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects."
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day the Heavenly Empress submitted a memorial arguing that the dynasty's sacred lineage descended from the Mysterious Primeval Emperor; she asked that nobles and officials study the Laozi and that the Mingjing examination each year include it alongside the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects."

sentences.zh: 又請「自今父在，為母服齊衰三年。

translations.literal: She also asked, "From now on, when the father is alive, one shall wear three years of unhemmed mourning for the mother.
translations.idiomatic: She also requested that henceforth, while the father lived, sons wear three years of unhemmed mourning for their mothers.

sentences.zh: 又，京官八品以上，宜量加俸祿。」

translations.literal: Further, capital officials of the eighth rank and above should receive increased salaries as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials of the eighth rank and above should receive appropriate salary increases."

sentences.zh: 及其餘便宜，合十二條。

translations.literal: Together with other expedient measures, twelve articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: With other practical proposals, there were twelve articles in all.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒美，皆行之。

translations.literal: Edicts praised them and all were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts praised the proposals and all were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 是歲，有劉曉者，上疏論選，以為：「今選曹以檢勘為公道，書判為得人，殊不知考其德行才能。

translations.literal: That year a certain Liu Xiao memorialized on selection, holding that: "Today the Selection Office takes document verification as fairness and written judgment as finding talent, yet does not know to examine virtue, conduct, and ability.
translations.idiomatic: That year a man named Liu Xiao submitted a memorial on official selection, arguing: "The Selection Office today treats document checks as fairness and written judgments as proof of talent, without truly examining virtue, conduct, or ability.

sentences.zh: 況書判借人者眾矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who borrow others' written judgments are many.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, many candidates borrow others' written judgments.

sentences.zh: 又，禮部取士，專用文章為甲乙，故天下之士，皆捨德行而趨文藝，有朝登甲科而夕陷刑辟者，雖日誦萬言，何關理體！

translations.literal: Again, the Ministry of Rites selects scholars solely by ranking compositions, so scholars throughout the realm all abandon virtue and conduct to pursue literary art; some who in the morning pass the highest grade by evening fall under penal law—though they recite ten thousand words a day, what has it to do with governing principle!
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites ranks candidates solely by literary composition, so scholars everywhere abandon moral cultivation for belles-lettres; some who pass the highest examinations in the morning face criminal punishment by evening—of what use are ten thousand words a day to the substance of governance!

sentences.zh: 文成七步，未足化人。

translations.literal: Even composing a piece in seven paces is insufficient to transform people.
translations.idiomatic: Even Cao Zhi's seven-pace poem was not enough to transform the world.

sentences.zh: 況盡心卉木之間，極筆煙霞之際，以斯成俗，豈非大謬！

translations.literal: How much less to devote one's heart among flowers and trees and exhaust one's brush in mist and clouds—to make this the custom, is it not a great error!
translations.idiomatic: How much less can a society flourish when scholars devote themselves to plants and landscapes and exhaust their pens on mist and clouds—to make this the norm is a grave mistake!

sentences.zh: 夫人之慕名，如水趨下，上有所好，下必甚焉。

translations.literal: For people to pursue reputation is like water flowing downward; when those above have a preference, those below surely exceed it.
translations.idiomatic: People pursue fame as water flows downhill; when the ruler favors something, his subjects inevitably carry it to excess.

sentences.zh: 陛下若取士以德行為先，文藝為末，則多士雷奔，四方風動矣！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty selects scholars with virtue and conduct first and literary art last, then many scholars will rush like thunder and the four quarters will stir like wind!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty selects officials with virtue and conduct first and literary skill last, worthy men will flock to court from every direction!"

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙寅，以于闐國為毘沙都督府，分其境內為十州，以于闐王尉遲伏闍雄為毘沙都督。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day bingyin: Khotan was made the Protectorate of Bisha; its territory was divided into ten prefectures; the king of Khotan Yuchi Fuzhanxiong was made Protector of Bisha.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the sixteenth day of the first month, Khotan was organized as the Bisha Protectorate, its territory divided into ten prefectures, with King Yuchi Fuzhanxiong of Khotan appointed protector.

sentences.zh: 辛末，吐蕃遣其大臣論吐渾彌來請和，且請與吐谷渾復修鄰好；

translations.literal: Day xinmo: Tibet sent its minister Lun Tuhunmi to request peace and also asked to restore neighborly friendship with the Tuyuhun;
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day Tibet sent its minister Lun Tuhunmi to sue for peace and to restore friendly relations with the Tuyuhun;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 二月，劉仁軌大破新羅之眾於七重城，又使靺鞨浮海略新羅之南境，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Second month: Liu Ren'gui greatly defeated Silla's forces at Chilseong Fortress, and also had the Mohe cross the sea to raid Silla's southern border, beheading and capturing very many.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Liu Ren'gui routed the Silla army at Chilseong Fortress and sent Mohe forces by sea to raid Silla's southern coast, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 仁軌引兵還。

translations.literal: Ren'gui led the troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Ren'gui then withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 詔以李謹行為安東鎮撫大使，屯新羅之買肖城以經略之，三戰皆捷，新羅乃遣使入貢，且謝罪；

translations.literal: An edict made Li Jinxing Pacification Commissioner of Andong, encamped at Silla's Maixiao City to oversee operations; in three battles he was victorious; Silla then sent envoys with tribute and also apologized;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinxing was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the East and encamped at Silla's Maixiao City; after three victories Silla sent envoys with tribute to apologize;

sentences.zh: 上赦之，復新羅王法敏官爵。

translations.literal: the emperor pardoned them and restored Silla king Fammin's offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor pardoned Silla and restored King Fammin's rank and titles.

sentences.zh: 金仁問中道而還，改封臨海郡公。

translations.literal: Kim Inmun returned halfway; he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Kim Inmun turned back en route and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁巳，天-{后}-祀先蠶於邙山之陽，百官及朝集使皆陪位。

translations.literal: Third month, day dingsi: the Heavenly Empress sacrificed to the Silkworm Ancestor on the south slope of Mount Mang; all officials and assembly envoys attended in supporting positions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the sixth day, the Heavenly Empress performed the silkworm rites on the south slope of Mount Mang, with all officials and tribute envoys in attendance.

sentences.zh: 上苦風眩甚，議使天-{后}-攝知國政。

translations.literal: The emperor suffered severely from dizzy spells; it was proposed that the Heavenly Empress administer state affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suffered severe dizzy spells, and courtiers proposed that the Heavenly Empress govern in his stead.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎同三品郝處俊曰：「天子理外，-{后}-理內，天之道也。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and of the third rank Hao Chujun said, "The Son of Heaven governs the outer, the empress governs the inner—this is Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Chujun, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor, said, "The Son of Heaven governs outward affairs and the empress inward affairs—that is Heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 昔魏文帝著令，雖有幼主，不許皇后臨朝，所以杜禍亂之萌也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Wei issued an order that even if there were a young ruler, the empress was not permitted to preside at court—thus to cut off the sprouting of calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei once decreed that even with a child emperor the empress must not preside at court, precisely to forestall disorder.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何以高祖、太宗之天下，不傳之子孫而委之天-{后}-乎！」

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty take the realm of Gaozu and Taizong and, instead of passing it to sons and grandsons, entrust it to the Heavenly Empress!"
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty entrust the realm won by Gaozu and Taizong not to your sons and grandsons but to the Heavenly Empress!"

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎昌樂李義琰曰：「處俊之言至忠，陛下宜聽之。」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yiyan of Changle said, "Chujun's words are utmost loyal; Your Majesty ought to heed them."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiyan of Changle, Vice Director of the Secretariat, said, "Chujun speaks with utmost loyalty; Your Majesty should heed him."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-多引文學之士著作郎元萬頃、左史劉禕之等，使之撰《列女傳》、《臣軌》、《百僚新戒》、《樂書》，幾千餘卷。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress drew in many men of literary talent—Editing Clerk Yuan Wanqing, Left Historian Liu Yizhi, and others—having them compile Biographies of Exemplary Women, Tracks of Ministers, New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials, and Books of Music, several thousand scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress recruited literary scholars such as Yuan Wanqing, Editing Clerk, and Liu Yizhi, Left Historian, commissioning them to compile the Biographies of Exemplary Women, Tracks of Ministers, New Admonitions for Officials, and Books of Music—several thousand scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 朝廷奏議及百司表疏，時密令參決，以分宰相之權，時人謂之北門學士。

translations.literal: On court memorials and reports from the hundred offices she sometimes secretly ordered them to participate in decisions, dividing the chancellors' power; contemporaries called them the North Gate Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: She secretly had them participate in decisions on court memorials and departmental reports, dividing the chancellors' authority; contemporaries called them the North Gate Academicians.

sentences.zh: 禕之，子翼之子也。

translations.literal: Yizhi was the son of Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was the son of Liu Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰，以司農少卿韋弘機為司農卿。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengchen: Vice Minister of the Court of the National Granaries Wei Hongji was made Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the second day of the fourth month, Wei Hongji, Vice Minister of the Court of the National Granaries, was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 弘機兼知東都營田，受詔完葺宮苑。

translations.literal: Hongji concurrently oversaw Eastern Capital garrison fields and received an edict to complete and repair the palace parks.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji also oversaw garrison agriculture in the Eastern Capital and was ordered to repair the palace parks.

sentences.zh: 有宦者於苑中犯法，弘機杖之，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: A eunuch violated the law in the park; Hongji beat him with the staff and only then reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch broke the law in the park, Hongji had him beaten with the staff before reporting to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上以為能，賜絹數十匹，曰：「更有犯者，卿即杖之，不必奏也。」

translations.literal: The emperor considered him capable and bestowed several dozen bolts of silk, saying, "If there are further offenders, you may beat them at once—no need to report."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his firmness, rewarded him with several dozen bolts of silk, and said, "If others offend, beat them at once—no need to report first."

sentences.zh: 初，左千牛將軍長安趙瑰尚高祖女常樂公主，生女為周王顯妃。

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Palace Interior General Zhao Gui of Chang'an married Emperor Gaozu's daughter Princess Changle and bore a daughter who became consort to Prince Zhou Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhao Gui of Chang'an, General of the Left Palace Interior Service, had married Princess Changle, daughter of Emperor Gaozu; their daughter became consort to Prince Zhou Xian.

sentences.zh: 公主頗為上所厚，天-{后}-惡之。

translations.literal: The princess was quite favored by the emperor; the Heavenly Empress hated her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess enjoyed the emperor's favor, which the Heavenly Empress resented.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，妃坐廢，幽閉於內侍省，食料給生者，防人候其突煙，已而數日煙不出，開視，死腐矣。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: the consort was deposed for her crime, confined in the Palace Domestic Service, with rations supplied to a living person; guards watched for smoke from her cooking fire; after several days no smoke issued; when they opened to look, she was dead and rotting.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day the consort was deposed and confined in the Palace Domestic Service; guards watched her cooking fire for signs of life, but after several days no smoke rose; when they entered, they found her dead and decomposing.

sentences.zh: 瑰自定州刺史貶括州刺史，令公主隨之官，仍絕其朝謁。

translations.literal: Gui was demoted from governor of Ding Prefecture to governor of Kuo Prefecture; the princess was ordered to follow him to his post, and their court audiences were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was demoted from governor of Ding Prefecture to Kuo Prefecture; the princess was sent with him and forbidden further court audiences.

sentences.zh: 太子弘仁孝謙謹，上甚愛之；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Hong was benevolent, filial, modest, and careful; the emperor greatly loved him;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Hong was benevolent, filial, modest, and dutiful, and the emperor loved him dearly;

sentences.zh: 禮接士大夫，中外屬心。

translations.literal: he treated scholar-officials with ritual courtesy; within and without all looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: he treated scholar-officials with courtesy, and men throughout the court looked to him with hope.

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-方逞其志，太子奏請，數迕旨，由是失愛於天-{后}-。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress was just then pursuing her aims; the crown prince's memorials and requests repeatedly went against her intent, and thereby he lost the Heavenly Empress's favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress was then pursuing her own designs; the crown prince's petitions repeatedly crossed her will, and he fell from her favor.

sentences.zh: 義陽、宣城二公主，蕭淑妃之女也，坐母得罪，幽於掖庭，年逾三十不嫁。

translations.literal: The two princesses Yiyang and Xuancheng, daughters of Consort Xiao Shufei, because their mother had been punished, were confined in the Rear Palace; past thirty they were still unmarried.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses Yiyang and Xuancheng, daughters of Consort Xiao Shufei, had been confined in the rear palace after their mother's disgrace and remained unmarried past thirty.

sentences.zh: 太子見之驚惻，遽奏請出降，上許之。

translations.literal: The crown prince saw them and was shocked and moved to pity; he hastily memorialized asking that they be released for marriage; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince saw them and was moved to pity; he immediately petitioned that they be released to marry, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-怒，即日以公主配當上翊衛權毅、王遂古。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress was angry and that same day married the princesses to Palace Guard attendants Quan Yi and Wang Suigu.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress was furious and that same day married them to the lowly guardsmen Quan Yi and Wang Suigu.

sentences.zh: 己亥，太子薨於合璧宮，時人以為天-{后}-鴆之也。

translations.literal: Day jihai: the crown prince died at Hebi Palace; people of the time believed the Heavenly Empress had poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day the crown prince died at Hebi Palace; contemporaries believed the Heavenly Empress had poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，車駕還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Day renyin: the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day the emperor returned to Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊申，下詔：「朕方欲禪位皇太子，而疾遽不起，宜申往命，加以尊名，可謚為孝敬皇帝。」

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wushen: an edict was issued: "We were just about to abdicate the throne to the crown prince, but illness suddenly did not lift; the former command should be proclaimed and an honored name added—he may be posthumously titled Emperor Xiaojing."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the ninth day, an edict declared: "We were on the point of abdicating to the crown prince when illness suddenly carried him off; let his former designation be proclaimed and an honored title added—he shall be posthumously titled Emperor Xiaojing."

sentences.zh: 六月，戊寅，立雍王賢為皇太子，赦天下。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day wuyin: Prince Yong Xian was established as crown prince; amnesty was granted to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the ninth day, Prince Yong Xian was made crown prince and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-惡慈州刺史杞王上金，有司希旨奏其罪；

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress hated Prince Qi Shangjin, governor of Ci Prefecture; the offices, seeking to please her intent, memorialized his crimes;
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress hated Prince Qi Shangjin, governor of Ci Prefecture; the authorities, reading her wishes, reported his crimes;

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，上金坐解官，澧州安置。

translations.literal: autumn, seventh month: Shangjin was punished by removal from office and resettlement in Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: in autumn, in the seventh month, he was stripped of office and exiled to Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，葬孝敬皇帝於恭陵。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day gengyin: Emperor Xiaojing was buried at Gongling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day, Emperor Xiaojing was buried at Gongling.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以戴至德為右僕射，庚子，以劉仁軌為左僕射，並同中書門下三品如故。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: Dai Zhide was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; day gengzi: Liu Ren'gui was made Left Vice Director, both remaining Grand Counselors of the Secretariat and Chancellery as before.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day Dai Zhide was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; on the eleventh day Liu Ren'gui was appointed Left Vice Director; both remained Grand Counselors as before.

sentences.zh: 張文瓘為侍中，郝處俊為中書令，李敬玄為吏部尚書兼左庶子，同中書門下三品如故。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenbi was made Palace Attendant; Hao Chujun was made Secretariat Director; Li Jingxuan was made Minister of Personnel and concurrent Left Junior Mentor, all remaining Grand Counselors as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenbi was made Palace Attendant, Hao Chujun Secretariat Director, and Li Jingxuan Minister of Personnel and Left Junior Mentor, all remaining Grand Counselors as before.

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌、戴志德更日受牒訴，仁軌常以美言許之，至德必據理難詰，未嘗與奪，實有冤結者，密為奏辨。

translations.literal: Liu Ren'gui and Dai Zhide received petitions on alternate days; Ren'gui often promised them with fine words, while Zhide always examined according to reason and pressed hard questions, never deciding give or take himself; when there were real knots of injustice, he secretly memorialized to clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ren'gui and Dai Zhide heard petitions on alternate days; Ren'gui often promised relief in kind words, while Zhide rigorously questioned each case and never decided on the spot, secretly memorializing the throne when he found genuine injustice.

sentences.zh: 由是時譽皆歸仁軌。

translations.literal: Thereby the reputation of the time all went to Ren'gui.
translations.idiomatic: Public praise therefore fell to Ren'gui.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，至德曰：「威福者人主之柄，人臣安得盜取之！」

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Zhide said, "Authority and favor are the handle of the ruler—how can a subject usurp them!"
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, Zhide said, "Authority and favor belong to the sovereign—how can a subject seize them!"

sentences.zh: 上聞，深重之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard this and esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 有老嫗欲詣仁軌陳牒，誤詣至德，至德覽之未終，嫗曰：「本謂是解事僕射，乃不解事僕射邪！

translations.literal: An old woman wished to present a petition to Ren'gui but mistakenly went to Zhide; Zhide had not finished reading when the woman said, "I thought this was the vice director who understands affairs—so it is the vice director who does not understand affairs!
translations.idiomatic: An old woman seeking Ren'gui mistakenly brought her petition to Zhide; before he finished reading, she said, "I thought you were the vice director who gets things done—so you're the one who doesn't!

sentences.zh: 歸我牒！」

translations.literal: Give back my petition!"
translations.idiomatic: Give back my petition!"

sentences.zh: 至德笑而授之。

translations.literal: Zhide smiled and handed it to her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhide smiled and returned it.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其長者。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him as an elder of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 文瓘時兼大理卿，囚聞改官，皆慟哭。

translations.literal: Wenbi was then concurrently Director of the Court of Judicial Review; prisoners hearing of his transfer all wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbi was also Director of the Court of Judicial Review; when prisoners heard of his transfer, they wept.

sentences.zh: 文瓘性嚴正，諸司奏議，多所糾駁，上甚委之。

translations.literal: Wenbi's nature was stern and upright; on memorials from the various offices he often corrected and rejected; the emperor greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbi was stern and upright, frequently correcting and rejecting departmental memorials, and the emperor relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，徙冀王輪為相王。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day renxu: Prince of Ji Lun was moved to Prince of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the twenty-second day of the first month, Prince Ji Lun was redesignated Prince Xiang.

sentences.zh: 納州獠反，敕黔州都督發兵討之。

translations.literal: Liao of Na Prefecture rebelled; an edict ordered the Protector of Qian Prefecture to raise troops and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao tribes of Na Prefecture rebelled; the Protector of Qian Prefecture was ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲戌，徙安東都護府於遼東故城；

translations.literal: Second month, day jiaxu: the Andong Protectorate was moved to the old city of Liaodong;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the fourteenth day, the Andong Protectorate was moved to the old city of Liaodong;

sentences.zh: 先是有華人任安東官者，悉罷之。

translations.literal: earlier there had been Chinese serving as Andong officials—all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: all Chinese who had held office under Andong were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 徙熊津都督府於建安故城；

translations.literal: the Xiongjin Protectorate was moved to the old city of Jian'an;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongjin Protectorate was moved to the old city of Jian'an;

sentences.zh: 其百濟戶口先徙於徐、兗等州者，皆置於建安。

translations.literal: Baekje households earlier moved to Xu, Yan, and other prefectures were all resettled at Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje populations previously relocated to Xu, Yan, and other prefectures were all resettled at Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-勸上封中岳；

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress urged the emperor to perform the Feng sacrifice at Mount Song;
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress urged the emperor to perform the Feng and Shan rites at Mount Song;

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔以今冬有事於嵩山。

translations.literal: day guiwei: an edict ordered that this winter ceremonies be held at Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-first day an edict announced rites at Mount Song that winter.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上幸汝州之溫湯。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: the emperor visited the hot springs of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day the emperor visited the hot springs of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸卯，黃門侍郎來恆、中書侍郎薛元超並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Third month, day guimao: Vice Director of the Chancellery Lai Heng and Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao were both made Grand Counselors of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the nineteenth day, Lai Heng, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Xue Yuanchao, Vice Director of the Secretariat, were both appointed Grand Counselors.

sentences.zh: 恆，濟之兄；

translations.literal: Heng was the elder brother of Jizhi;
translations.idiomatic: Heng was the elder brother of Lai Jizhi;

sentences.zh: 元超，收之子也。

translations.literal: Yuanchao was the son of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchao was the son of Xue Shou.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，上還東都。

translations.literal: Day jiachen: the emperor returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day the emperor returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 閏月，吐蕃寇鄯、廓、河、芳等州，敕左監門衛中郎將令狐智通發興、鳳等州兵以御之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month: Tibet raided Shan, Kuo, He, Fang, and other prefectures; an edict ordered Central Commander of the Left Gate Guards Linghu Zhitong to raise troops from Xing, Feng, and other prefectures to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Tibet raided Shan, Kuo, He, Fang, and other prefectures; Linghu Zhitong, Central Commander of the Left Gate Guards, was ordered to raise troops from Xing, Feng, and other prefectures to repel them.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔以吐蕃犯塞，停封中岳。

translations.literal: Day jimao: an edict ordered that because Tibet had violated the frontier, the Feng sacrifice at the Central Peak was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day an edict announced that the Feng rite at the Central Peak would be suspended because Tibet had raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以洛州牧周王顯為洮州道行軍元帥，將工部尚書劉審禮等十二總管，并州大都督相王輪為涼州道行軍元帥，將左衛大將軍契苾何力等，以討吐蕃。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Prince Zhou Xian, Governor of Luo Prefecture, was made Field Marshal of the Taozhou Circuit, leading twelve overall commanders including Liu Shenli, Minister of Works; Prince Xiang Lun, Governor-General of Bing Prefecture, was made Field Marshal of the Liangzhou Circuit, leading Left Guard General-in-Chief Qibi Heli and others, to attack Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day Prince Zhou Xian of Luo was appointed field marshal of the Taozhou route with twelve overall commanders under him, including Minister of Works Liu Shenli; Prince Xiang Lun, governor-general of Bing, was made field marshal of the Liangzhou route with Left Guard General Qibi Heli and others, to chastise Tibet.

sentences.zh: 二王皆不行。

translations.literal: Both princes declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: Neither prince would take the field.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，車駕西還。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: the imperial carriage returned west.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day the emperor's procession turned westward.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，中書侍郎李義琰同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Day jiayin: Li Yiyan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifty-first day Li Yiyan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 戊午，車駕至九成宮。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: the imperial carriage arrived at Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifty-fifth day the emperor reached Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸亥，黃門侍郎晉陵高智周同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day guihai: Gao Zhizhou of Jinling, Vice Director of the Chancellery, was made Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the sixtieth day, Gao Zhizhou of Jinling, Vice Director of the Chancellery, was appointed Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙未，吐蕃寇疊州。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day yiwei: Tibet raided Die Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the twenty-second day of the eighth month, Tibet attacked Die Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，敕：「桂、廣、交、黔等都督府，比來注擬土人，簡擇未精，自今每四年遣五品已上清正官充使，仍令御史同往注擬。」

translations.literal: Day renyin: an edict stated: "For the Protectorates-General of Gui, Guang, Jiao, Qian, and others, in recent years local men have been nominated for appointment, but selection has not been careful; from now on every four years officials of the fifth rank and above who are upright and pure shall be sent as commissioners, and censors shall accompany them to make nominations."
translations.idiomatic: On the thirty-ninth day an edict declared: "At the Protectorates-General of Gui, Guang, Jiao, Qian, and the like, local candidates have lately been proposed without careful vetting; henceforth every four years upright officials of fifth rank or higher shall serve as commissioners, with censors sent along to supervise nominations."

sentences.zh: 時人謂之南選。

translations.literal: People of the time called this the Southern Selection.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries called it the Southern Selection.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬申，大理奏左威衛大將軍權善才、右監門中郎將范懷義誤斫昭陵柏，罪當除名；

translations.literal: Ninth month, day renshen: the Court of Judicial Review reported that Left Weirui Guard General-in-Chief Quan Shancai and Right Gate Commandant Fan Huaiyi had mistakenly cut down cypress trees at Zhaoling; the crime warranted dismissal from office;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the ninth day, the Court of Judicial Review reported that Quan Shancai, General-in-Chief of the Left Weirui Guard, and Fan Huaiyi, Right Gate Commandant, had accidentally felled cypresses at Zhaoling—a offense meriting removal from office;

sentences.zh: 上特命殺之。

translations.literal: the emperor specially ordered them executed.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor personally ordered their execution.

sentences.zh: 大理丞太原狄仁傑奏：「二人罪不當死。」

translations.literal: Di Renjie of Taiyuan, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, submitted: "The crime of the two men does not warrant death."
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie of Taiyuan, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, memorialized: "These two men do not deserve death."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善才等斫陵柏，我不殺則為不孝。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shancai and the others cut down tomb cypresses—if I do not kill them I would be unfilial."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Shancai and his fellows chopped down tomb cypresses—if I spare them I am unfilial."

sentences.zh: 仁傑固執不已，上作色，令出，仁傑曰：「犯顏直諫，自古以為難。

translations.literal: Renjie persisted unyieldingly; the emperor showed anger and ordered him out. Renjie said: "To risk one's face and speak blunt remonstrance has always been considered difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie would not yield; the emperor flushed with anger and ordered him dismissed. Renjie said, "To speak blunt truth to one's ruler has always been hard.

sentences.zh: 臣以為遇桀、紂則難，遇堯、舜則易。

translations.literal: I believe that with Jie and Zhou it would be difficult, but with Yao and Shun it would be easy.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that it is hard before a Jie or Zhou, but easy before a Yao or Shun.

sentences.zh: 今法不至死而陛下特殺之，是法不信於人也，人何所措其手足！

translations.literal: Now the law does not reach death yet Your Majesty specially executes them—this means the law is not trusted by the people; where are people to place their hands and feet!
translations.idiomatic: The law stops short of death, yet Your Majesty would kill them anyway—the law will no longer bind anyone; what will people do with their hands and feet!

sentences.zh: 且張釋之有言：『設有盜長陵一抔土，陛下何以處之？』

translations.literal: Moreover Zhang Shizhi once said: 'If someone stole a handful of earth from Changling, how would Your Majesty deal with it?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizhi once asked: 'Suppose a man stole one scoop of soil from Changling—what would Your Majesty do?'

sentences.zh: 今以一株柏殺二將軍，後代謂陛下為何如矣？

translations.literal: Now for a single cypress tree you execute two generals—what will later generations say of Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now two generals die for one cypress—what will posterity think of Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 臣不敢奉詔者，恐陷陛下於不道，且羞見釋之於地下故也。」

translations.literal: I dare not obey the edict because I fear leading Your Majesty into wrongdoing, and also because I would be ashamed to face Shizhi in the netherworld."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot obey because I fear dragging Your Majesty into injustice, and because I would be ashamed to meet Shizhi beneath the earth."

sentences.zh: 上怒稍解，二人除名，流嶺南。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger eased somewhat; the two men were dismissed from office and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath softened; the two were stripped of rank and exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 後數日，擢仁傑為侍御史。

translations.literal: Several days later Renjie was promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Renjie was raised to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，仁傑為并州法曹，同僚鄭崇質當使絕域。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Renjie was Legal Administrator of Bing Prefecture, his colleague Zheng Chongzhi was due to be sent to a distant region.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Renjie served as Legal Administrator of Bing Prefecture, his colleague Zheng Chongzhi was assigned a mission to a far frontier.

sentences.zh: 崇質母老且病，仁傑曰：「彼母如此，豈可使之有萬里之憂！」

translations.literal: Chongzhi's mother was old and ill; Renjie said: "With his mother in such condition, how can we let him bear the worry of ten thousand li!"
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi's mother was aged and sick; Renjie said, "His mother is in such straits—how can we send him ten thousand li away in anxiety!"

sentences.zh: 詣長史藺仁基，請代之行。

translations.literal: He went to Chief Administrator Lin Renji and asked to go in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Chief Administrator Lin Renji and volunteered to go in Chongzhi's place.

sentences.zh: 仁基素與司馬李孝廉不葉，因相謂曰：「吾輩豈可不自愧乎！」

translations.literal: Renji had long been at odds with Military Administrator Li Xiaolian; they said to each other: "How can we not feel ashamed of ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Renji had long been estranged from Military Administrator Li Xiaolian; they said to one another, "Are we not ashamed of ourselves!"

sentences.zh: 遂相與輯睦。

translations.literal: Thereupon they became reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: From that day they made peace.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，祫享太廟，用太學博士史璨議，禘後三年而祫，祫後二年而禘。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: a joint seasonal offering was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; following the proposal of Erudite of the Imperial Academy Shi Can, three years after a di rite there should be a xia rite, and two years after a xia rite there should be a di rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirty-fourth day a xia offering was held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; adopting the proposal of Imperial Academy Erudite Shi Can, a xia rite would follow a di rite after three years, and a di rite after a xia rite after two.

sentences.zh: 郇王素節，蕭淑妃之子也，警敏好學。

translations.literal: Prince Su of Xun, son of Consort Xiao, was sharp-witted and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Su of Xun, born of Consort Xiao, was quick-witted and eager to learn.

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-惡之，自岐州刺史左遷申州刺史。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress hated him and demoted him from Prefect of Qi Prefecture to Prefect of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress disliked him and transferred him from prefect of Qi to prefect of Shen.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，敕曰：「素節既有舊疾，不須入朝。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng, an edict stated: "Su-jie has a chronic illness and need not come to court."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfeng era an edict read, "Su-jie suffers a longstanding illness and need not attend court."

sentences.zh: 而素節實無疾，自以久不得入覲，乃著《忠孝論》。

translations.literal: But Su-jie actually had no illness; because he had long been unable to attend audience, he wrote Discourse on Loyalty and Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: In truth he was not ill; barred from audience for so long, he composed a Discourse on Loyalty and Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 王府倉曹參軍張柬之因使潛封其論以進。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi, Warehouse Adjutant of the Prince's Household, while on mission secretly sealed his treatise and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi, a warehouse adjutant in the prince's household, on an official journey secretly forwarded the treatise sealed.

sentences.zh: 後見之，誣以贓賄，丙午，降封翻陽王，袁州安置。

translations.literal: When the empress saw it, she falsely charged him with bribery; on day bingwu he was demoted to Prince of Fanyang and settled at Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress read it she framed him for bribery; on the forty-third day he was reduced to Prince of Fanyang and confined at Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬申，改元，赦天下。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day renshen: the era name was changed and an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the ninth day, the reign title was changed and the realm was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以李敬玄為中書令。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: Li Jingxuan was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day Li Jingxuan was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊午，以來恆為河南道大使，薛元超為河北道大使，尚書左丞鄢陵崔知悌、國子司業鄭祖玄為江南道大使，分道巡撫。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day wuwu: Lai Heng was made commissioner of Henan Circuit, Xue Yuanchao commissioner of Hebei Circuit, Cui Zhiti of Yanling, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Zheng Zuxuan, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, commissioners of Jiangnan Circuit, each touring and inspecting by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the fifty-fifth day, Lai Heng was named Henan circuit commissioner, Xue Yuanchao Hebei commissioner, Cui Zhiti of Yanling and Zheng Zuxuan, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, Jiangnan commissioners—they fanned out to tour and inspect.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，上耕籍田。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day yihai: the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the twelfth day of the first month, the emperor performed the plowing rite in the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 初，劉仁軌引兵自熊津還，扶餘隆畏新羅之逼，不敢留，尋亦還朝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Ren'gui withdrew his troops from Xiongjin; Buyeo Rong, fearing pressure from Silla, dared not remain and soon also returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Ren'gui had led his army back from Xiongjin; Buyeo Rong, fearing Silla's pressure, dared not stay and soon returned to court as well.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁巳，以工部尚書高藏為遼東州都督，封朝鮮王，遣歸遼東，安輯高麗餘眾；

translations.literal: Second month, day dingsi: Gao Zang, Minister of Works, was made Governor of Liaodong Prefecture, enfeoffed as King of Goryeo, and sent back to Liaodong to pacify and gather the remaining Goryeo people;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the fifty-fourth day, Minister of Works Gao Zang was made governor of Liaodong, enfeoffed King of Goryeo, and sent back to Liaodong to settle the Goryeo remnant;

sentences.zh: 高麗先在諸州者，皆遣與藏俱歸。

translations.literal: Goryeo people already in various prefectures were all sent to return together with Zang.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo folk already scattered among the prefectures were all ordered home with Zang.

sentences.zh: 又以司農卿扶餘隆為熊津都督，封帶方王，亦遣歸安輯百濟餘眾，仍移安東都護府於新城以統之。

translations.literal: Buyeo Rong, Minister of Revenue, was also made Protector of Xiongjin, enfeoffed as King of Daifang, likewise sent back to pacify the remaining Baekje people, and the Andong Protectorate was moved to Xincheng to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo Rong, Minister of Revenue, was made Protector of Xiongjin and enfeoffed King of Daifang, likewise sent to pacify Baekje's remnant; the Andong Protectorate was shifted to Xincheng to command them.

sentences.zh: 時百濟荒殘，命隆寓居高麗之境。

translations.literal: At the time Baekje was desolate and ruined, so Rong was ordered to reside within Goryeo territory.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje lay in ruins, so Rong was lodged within Goryeo's borders.

sentences.zh: 藏至遼東，謀叛，潛與靺鞨通；

translations.literal: When Zang reached Liaodong, he plotted rebellion and secretly communicated with the Mohe;
translations.idiomatic: Once in Liaodong, Zang plotted revolt and secretly treated with the Mohe;

sentences.zh: 召還，徙邛州而死，散徙其人於河南、隴右諸州，貧者留安東城傍。

translations.literal: He was recalled, exiled to Qiong Prefecture, and died there; his people were scattered and resettled in Henan, Longyou, and other prefectures, while the poor were left near Andong city.
translations.idiomatic: recalled, exiled to Qiong, and died there; his followers were dispersed to Henan, Longyou, and other prefectures, the poor left by Andong's walls.

sentences.zh: 高麗舊城沒於新羅，餘眾散入靺鞨及突厥，隆亦竟不敢還故地，高氏、扶餘氏遂亡。

translations.literal: Goryeo's old cities fell to Silla; the remaining people scattered into Mohe and the Turks; Rong in the end dared not return to his old lands—the Gao and Buyeo lines thus perished.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo's old seats were swallowed by Silla; survivors drifted into Mohe and Turk lands; Rong never dared return—the Gao and Buyeo houses were extinguished.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸亥朔，以郝處俊、高智周並為左庶子，李義琰為右庶子。

translations.literal: Third month, first day guihai: Hao Chujun and Gao Zhizhou were both made Left Subscribers, Li Yiyan Right Subscriber.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month Hao Chujun and Gao Zhizhou were both appointed Left Subscribers and Li Yiyan Right Subscriber.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，左庶子張大安同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Zhang Da'an, Left Subscriber, was made Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Left Subscriber Zhang Da'an was made Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 大安，公謹之子也。
