translations.literal: Da'an was the son of Gongjin.
translations.idiomatic: Da'an was the son of Zhang Gongjin.

sentences.zh: 詔以河南、北旱，遣御史中丞崔謐等分道存問賑給。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that because Henan and Hebei were suffering drought, Censor-in-Chief Cui Mi and others be sent by separate routes to inquire after the people and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict, citing drought in Henan and Hebei, dispatched Censor-in-Chief Cui Mi and others by separate routes to inquire after the people and distribute relief.

sentences.zh: 侍御史寧陵劉思立上疏，以為：「今麥秀蠶老，農事方殷，敕使撫巡，人皆竦手卞，忘其家業，冀此天恩，聚集參迎，妨廢不少。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Liu Sili of Ningling submitted a memorial arguing: "Now wheat is in ear and silkworms are mature—the farm work is at its busiest; when imperial envoys tour to comfort the people, everyone stands stiffly with folded hands, forgets his household work, and gathers to welcome them in hope of heavenly grace—considerable hindrance and waste.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Liu Sili of Ningling submitted that "wheat now stands in ear and silkworms are aging—the height of farm season; when imperial envoys come to comfort the people, folk stand rigid with folded hands, abandon their households, and throng to greet them hoping for grace—much work is lost.

sentences.zh: 既緣賑給，須立簿書，本欲安存，更成煩擾。

translations.literal: Because relief is involved, ledgers must be kept—what was meant to secure the people's welfare becomes further vexation.
translations.idiomatic: Relief demands registers and paperwork; what should save lives only adds trouble.

sentences.zh: 望且委州縣賑給，待秋深務閒，出使褒貶。」

translations.literal: I ask that relief for now be entrusted to prefectures and counties, and that after autumn deep when work is slack, envoys be sent to praise and censure."
translations.idiomatic: Let prefectures and counties handle relief for now; send envoys to reward and punish only after autumn's labors ease."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，謐等遂不行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Mi and the others did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was accepted and Mi's mission was canceled.

sentences.zh: 五月，吐蕃寇扶州之臨河鎮，擒鎮將杜孝升，令繼書說松州都督武居寂使降，考升固執不從。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Tibet raided Linhe Fort in Fu Prefecture, captured Fort Commander Du Xiaosheng, and had him write a letter persuading Wu Juji, Protector of Song Prefecture, to surrender; Xiaosheng steadfastly refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Tibet struck Linhe Fort in Fu Prefecture, seized its commander Du Xiaosheng, and made him write urging Song Protector Wu Juji to surrender; Xiaosheng held firm and would not obey.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃軍還，捨孝升而去，孝升復帥餘眾拒守。

translations.literal: When the Tibetan army withdrew, they released Xiaosheng and left; Xiaosheng again led the remaining troops in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans withdrew they let Xiaosheng go; he rallied the remnant and held on.

sentences.zh: 詔以孝升為游擊將軍。

translations.literal: An edict made Xiaosheng Mobile Corps General.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Xiaosheng to Mobile Corps General.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，徙周王顯為英王，更名哲。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: Prince Zhou Xian was moved to Prince Ying and renamed Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Prince Zhou Xian became Prince Ying and took the name Zhe.

sentences.zh: 命劉仁軌鎮洮河軍。

translations.literal: Liu Ren'gui was ordered to garrison the Taohe Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ren'gui was ordered to hold the Taohe Army.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，乙卯，詔大發兵討吐蕃。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, day yimao: an edict ordered a massive mobilization to attack Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the yimao day of the twelfth month, an edict ordered a massive mobilization against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 詔以顯慶新禮，多不師古，其五禮並依《周禮》行事。

translations.literal: An edict held that the new rites of Xianqing in many respects did not follow antiquity; all five categories of rite were to follow the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that the Xianqing ritual code often ignored antiquity; henceforth all five rites would follow the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 自是禮官益無憑守，每有大禮，臨時撰定。

translations.literal: From this the ritual officials increasingly had nothing fixed to rely on; whenever there was a major ceremony, it was drafted and settled on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers thereafter lacked fixed standards; every great ceremony was improvised on the day.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，百官及蠻夷酋長朝天-{后}-於光順門。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day xinyou: all officials and tribal chieftains attended audience on the Heavenly Empress at Guangshun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the fifty-eighth day of the first month, officials and barbarian chiefs attended the Heavenly Empress at Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌鎮洮河，每有奏請，多為李敬玄所抑，由是怨之。

translations.literal: Liu Ren'gui garrisoned Taohe; whenever he submitted requests they were mostly blocked by Li Jingxuan, and for this reason he resented him.
translations.idiomatic: At Taohe, Liu Ren'gui found his petitions repeatedly stifled by Li Jingxuan—and came to hate him for it.

sentences.zh: 仁軌知敬玄非將帥才，欲中傷之，奏言：「西邊鎮守，非敬玄莫可。」

translations.literal: Ren'gui knew Jingxuan was no general's talent and wished to harm him; he submitted: "For guarding the western frontier, no one but Jingxuan will do."
translations.idiomatic: Ren'gui knew Jingxuan was no soldier and sought to ruin him; he memorialized, "The western frontier cannot be held without Jingxuan."

sentences.zh: 敬玄固辭，上曰：「仁軌須朕，朕亦自往，卿安得辭！」

translations.literal: Jingxuan firmly declined; the emperor said: "If Ren'gui needs me, I would go myself—how can you decline!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan refused; the emperor said, "If Ren'gui needed me I would go myself—how dare you refuse!"

sentences.zh: 丙子，以敬玄代仁軌為洮河道大總管兼安撫大使，仍檢校鄯州都督。

translations.literal: On day bingzi Jingxuan replaced Ren'gui as Grand Overall Commander of the Taozhou Circuit and concurrently Pacification Commissioner, and was also made acting Protector of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day Jingxuan replaced Ren'gui as grand commander of the Taozhou route and Pacification Commissioner, and was made acting Protector of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 又命益州大都督府長史李孝逸等發劍南、山南兵以赴之。

translations.literal: Li Xiaoyi, Chief Administrator of the Yi Prefecture Protectorate-General, and others were also ordered to raise troops from Jiannan and Shannan to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoyi, chief administrator of the Yi Protectorate-General, and others were ordered to levy Jiannan and Shannan troops to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 孝逸，神通之子也。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi was the son of Li Shentong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi was the son of Li Shentong.

sentences.zh: 癸未，遣左金吾將軍曹懷舜等分往河南、北募猛士，不問布衣及仕宦。

translations.literal: Day guiwei: Left Golden Guards General Cao Huaishun and others were sent by separate routes to Henan and Hebei to recruit fierce warriors, without distinction between commoners and officeholders.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day Left Golden Guards General Cao Huaishun and others were dispatched to Henan and Hebei to recruit bold fighters, commoner or official alike.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊申，赦天下，改來年元為通乾。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day wushen: an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm and the next year's era name was changed to Tongqian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the forty-fifth day, the realm was pardoned and the coming year was named Tongqian.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌，上幸九成宮。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day renxu: the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifty-ninth day of the fifth month the emperor went to Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，山中雨，大寒，從兵有凍死者。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: rain fell in the mountains and the cold was severe; some of the accompanying soldiers froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day rain swept the mountains in bitter cold, and some of the escort froze to death.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，李敬玄奏破吐蕃於龍支。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Li Jingxuan reported defeating Tibet at Longzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Li Jingxuan reported a victory over Tibet at Longzhi.

sentences.zh: 上初即位，不忍觀《破陣樂》，命撤之。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, he could not bear to watch Breaking the Battle Array and ordered it removed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign the emperor could not bear to watch Breaking the Battle Array and had it withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，太常少卿韋萬石奏：「久寢不作，懼成廢缺。

translations.literal: Day xinyou: Wei Wanshi, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, submitted: "Long unperformed, I fear it will fall into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifty-eighth day Wei Wanshi, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized, "It has long lain silent; I fear it will be lost.

sentences.zh: 請自今大宴會復奏之。」

translations.literal: I ask that from now on at grand banquets it be performed again."
translations.idiomatic: Let it be played again at great banquets from this day forward."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛酉，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day xinyou: the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the fifty-eighth day, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上將發兵討新羅，侍中張文瓘臥疾在家，自輿入見，諫曰：「今吐蕃為寇，方發兵西討；

translations.literal: The emperor was about to dispatch troops to attack Silla; Zhang Wenguan, Palace Attendant, lay ill at home but had himself carried in a litter to audience and remonstrated: "Now Tibet is raiding and troops are being sent west to chastise them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preparing to march against Silla when Zhang Wenguan, Palace Attendant, ill at home, had himself borne in a litter to remonstrate: "Tibet is raiding and we are already sending armies west;

sentences.zh: 新羅雖云不順，未嘗犯邊，若又東征，臣恐公私不堪其弊。」

translations.literal: Silla may be said to be rebellious, but it has never violated the frontier; if we campaign east as well, I fear public and private resources cannot bear the strain."
translations.idiomatic: Silla may be unruly, yet it has not crossed our borders; a second war to the east will break public and private strength alike."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，文瓘薨。

translations.literal: Day guihai: Wenguan died.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixtieth day Wenguan died.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，李敬玄將兵十八萬與吐蕃將論欽陵戰於青海之上，兵敗，工部尚書、左衛大將軍彭城僖公劉審禮為吐蕃所虜。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: Li Jingxuan led one hundred eighty thousand troops to battle the Tibetan general Lun Qinling on the shores of Qinghai; the army was defeated, and Liu Shenli, Minister of Works, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, Duke of Pengcheng with the posthumous name Xi, was captured by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day Li Jingxuan led one hundred eighty thousand men against the Tibetan general Lun Qinling beside Qinghai; the army was routed, and Liu Shenli, Minister of Works, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, Duke Xi of Pengcheng, was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 時審禮將前軍深入，頓於濠所，為虜所攻，敬玄懦怯，按兵不救。

translations.literal: At the time Shenli commanded the vanguard and advanced deep, encamping at a moated position; he was attacked by the enemy, but Jingxuan, timid and cowardly, held his troops back and did not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenli had led the vanguard deep in and camped behind ditches; when the enemy struck, Jingxuan, timorous, held his men and would not aid him.

sentences.zh: 聞審禮戰沒，狼狽還走，頓於承風嶺，阻泥溝以自固，虜屯兵高岡以壓之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Shenli had fallen in battle, he fled in disarray, encamping at Chengfeng Ridge and blocking muddy gullies to secure himself, while the enemy stationed troops on high ridges to press him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Shenli was lost, he fled in disorder to Chengfeng Ridge, damming muddy ravines for defense while the enemy massed on the heights above him.

sentences.zh: 左領軍員外將軍黑齒常之，夜帥敢死之士五百人襲擊虜營，虜眾潰亂，其將跋地設引兵遁去，敬玄乃收餘眾還鄯州。

translations.literal: Heichi Changzhi, Supernumerary General of the Left Army, by night led five hundred death-defying men in a surprise attack on the enemy camp; the enemy forces broke in disorder, their general Badeshi withdrew his troops and fled, and Jingxuan then gathered the remaining forces and returned to Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heichi Changzhi, supernumerary general of the Left Army, led five hundred dare-to-die men in a night raid on the enemy camp; the host broke, their general Badeshi fled, and Jingxuan gathered the remnant back to Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 審禮諸子自縛詣闕，請入吐蕃贖其父；

translations.literal: Shenli's sons bound themselves and came to the palace gate, asking to enter Tibet to ransom their father;
translations.idiomatic: Shenli's sons bound themselves and came to court, begging leave to enter Tibet and ransom their father;

sentences.zh: 敕聽次子易從詣吐蕃省之。

translations.literal: an edict permitted the second son Yicong to go to Tibet to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor allowed the second son, Yicong, to go to Tibet to see him.

sentences.zh: 比至，審禮已病卒，易從晝夜號哭不絕聲；

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Shenli had already died of illness; Yicong wept day and night without pause;
translations.idiomatic: When Yicong arrived, Shenli had already died of illness; he wailed day and night without cease;

sentences.zh: 吐蕃哀之，還其屍，易從徒跣負之以歸。

translations.literal: Tibet took pity on him, returned the corpse, and Yicong went barefoot and carried it home on his back.
translations.idiomatic: the Tibetans were moved, returned the body, and Yicong walked barefoot carrying his father home.

sentences.zh: 上嘉黑齒常之之功，擢拜左武衛將軍，充河源軍副使。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Heichi Changzhi's achievement, promoted him to General of the Left Martial Guard, and appointed him deputy commander of the Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Heichi Changzhi, promoting him to General of the Left Martial Guard and deputy commander of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 李敬玄之西征也，監察御史原武婁師德應猛士詔從軍，及敗，敕師德收集散亡，軍乃復振。

translations.literal: When Li Jingxuan marched west, Supervising Censor Lou Shide of Yuanwu responded to the edict recruiting fierce warriors and joined the campaign; after the defeat, an edict ordered Shide to gather the scattered and lost, and the army was thereby revived.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxuan marched west, Supervising Censor Lou Shide of Yuanwu answered the call for fierce warriors; after the rout an edict set him to gathering the scattered, and the army rallied.

sentences.zh: 因命使於吐蕃，吐蕃將論贊婆迎之赤嶺。

translations.literal: He was then ordered as envoy to Tibet; the Tibetan general Lun Zanpo received him at Chiling.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent as envoy to Tibet, where the general Lun Zanpo met him at Chiling.

sentences.zh: 師德宣導上意，諭以禍福，贊婆甚悅，為之數年不犯邊。

translations.literal: Shide conveyed the emperor's intent and expounded on fortune and calamity; Zanpo was greatly pleased and for several years did not violate the frontier on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Shide laid out the emperor's mind and the balance of fortune and ruin; Zanpo was well pleased and for years kept the peace on his account.

sentences.zh: 師德遷殿中侍御史，充河源軍司馬，兼知營田事。

translations.literal: Shide was transferred to Palace Attending Censor, appointed Army Administrator of the Heyuan Army, and concurrently charged with military colony affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shide was moved to Palace Attending Censor, made army administrator of Heyuan, and put in charge of military colonies.

sentences.zh: 上以吐蕃為憂，悉召侍臣謀之，或欲和親以息民；

translations.literal: Because the emperor was troubled by Tibet, he summoned all attending ministers to deliberate; some wished to seek a marriage alliance to give the people rest;
translations.idiomatic: Troubled by Tibet, the emperor convened his ministers; some favored marriage alliance to let the people breathe;

sentences.zh: 或欲嚴設守備，俟公私富實而討之；

translations.literal: some wished to fortify defenses strictly and wait until public and private stores were ample before attacking;
translations.idiomatic: others urged strong defenses until treasury and household alike were full, then strike;

sentences.zh: 或欲亟發兵擊之。

translations.literal: some wished to dispatch troops at once to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: still others wanted immediate war.

sentences.zh: 議竟不決，賜食而遣之。

translations.literal: The deliberation in the end reached no decision; he was granted food and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: No decision was reached; the man was fed and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 太學生宋城魏元忠上封事，言御吐蕃之策，以為：「理國之要，在文與武。

translations.literal: Songcheng Wei Yuanzhong, a student of the Imperial Academy, submitted a sealed memorial on strategy for resisting Tibet, holding that: "The essentials of governing a state lie in civil and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong of Songcheng, a student at the Imperial Academy, submitted a sealed memorial on how to meet the Tibetan threat, arguing that governing a state depends on both civil and military strength.

sentences.zh: 今言文者則以辭華為首而不及經綸，言武者則以騎射為先而不知方略，是皆何益於理亂哉！

translations.literal: Now those who speak of civil affairs take literary elegance as foremost and do not reach statecraft; those who speak of military affairs take horsemanship and archery as primary and do not know strategy—what good are any of these for order or chaos!
translations.idiomatic: Today civil men prize ornament over governance, and soldiers prize riding and shooting over strategy—what use are such men in deciding whether the realm stands or falls?

sentences.zh: 故陸機著《辨亡》之論，無救河橋之敗，養由基射穿七札，不濟鄢陵之師，此已然之明效也。

translations.literal: Thus Lu Ji wrote the essay "On Perishing," yet it did not save the defeat at Heqiao; Yang Youji's arrow pierced seven layers of hide, yet it did not aid the army at Yanling—these are already clear proofs made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's essay On Perishing did not avert disaster at Heqiao; Yang Youji's arrow pierced seven layers of hide, yet the army still failed at Yanling—history has already shown where fine words and fine shooting lead.

sentences.zh: 古語有之：『人無常俗，政有理亂；

translations.literal: An old saying runs: "People have no fixed customs; government has order and chaos;
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said: "Men are not bound to one way of life; governments rise and fall;

sentences.zh: 兵無強弱，將有巧拙。』

translations.literal: armies have no fixed strength or weakness; generals have skill and clumsiness."
translations.idiomatic: armies are not strong or weak by nature; generals are skilled or clumsy."

sentences.zh: 故選將當以智略為本，勇力為末。

translations.literal: Therefore in choosing generals one should take wisdom and strategy as the root, courage and strength as the least.
translations.idiomatic: So in choosing commanders, wit and strategy must come first, courage and brute force last.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷用人，類取將門子弟及死事之家，彼皆庸人，豈足當閫外之任！

translations.literal: Now in employing men the court generally takes sons of general families and households of those who died in service—they are all mediocre men; how can they suffice for duties beyond the gate!
translations.idiomatic: The court now fills its ranks with sons of generals and kin of the war dead—mediocrities all—and expects them to hold command beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 李左車、陳湯、呂蒙、孟觀，皆出貧賤而立殊功，未聞其家代為將也。

translations.literal: Li Zuoche, Chen Tang, Lü Meng, and Meng Guan all rose from poverty and low station to establish extraordinary merit; one never heard that their families for generations served as generals.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zuoche, Chen Tang, Lü Meng, and Meng Guan came up from nothing and won great fame; none of their houses had bred generals for generations.

sentences.zh: 「夫賞罰者，軍國之切務，苟有功不賞，有罪不誅，雖堯、舜不能以致理。

translations.literal: "Now rewards and punishments are the urgent business of army and state; if merit goes unrewarded and guilt goes unpunished, even Yao and Shun could not bring about good order.
translations.idiomatic: "Rewards and punishments are the lifeblood of army and state. If merit goes unrewarded and guilt unpunished, not even Yao and Shun could govern well.

sentences.zh: 議者皆云：『近日征伐，虛有賞格而無事實。』

translations.literal: Those in deliberation all say: "In recent campaigns there are empty reward scales but no actual fulfillment."
translations.idiomatic: Every voice at court says the same: recent campaigns promised rewards on paper that were never paid."

sentences.zh: 蓋由小才之吏不知大體，徒惜勳庸，恐虛倉庫。

translations.literal: This is because petty officials of small talent do not know the larger pattern, merely cherishing meritorious records and fearing to empty the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Petty clerks, blind to the larger stakes, hoard credit for the dead and fear to open the treasury.

sentences.zh: 不知士不用命，所損幾何！

translations.literal: They do not know that when soldiers refuse to obey orders, how much is lost!
translations.idiomatic: They never reckon what it costs when soldiers refuse to fight.

sentences.zh: 黔首雖微，不可欺罔。

translations.literal: The black-haired people, though humble, cannot be deceived.
translations.idiomatic: The common people may be lowly, but they are not fools.

sentences.zh: 豈得懸不信之令，設虛賞之科，而望其立功乎！

translations.literal: How can one post untrustworthy orders, set up empty reward statutes, and yet expect men to achieve merit!
translations.idiomatic: How can the throne post hollow promises and empty bounties and still expect men to die for it?

sentences.zh: 自蘇定方征遼東，李勣破平壤，賞絕不行，勳仍淹滯，不聞斬一台郎，戮一令史，以謝勳人。

translations.literal: Since Su Dingfang's eastern campaign against Liaodong and Li Ji's capture of Pyongyang, rewards have utterly gone unfulfilled and honors still languish; one never heard of beheading one bureau secretary or executing one clerk to answer the meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: Since Su Dingfang marched on Liaodong and Li Ji took Pyongyang, promised rewards have gone unpaid and honors have stalled—yet not one petty clerk was punished to appease the men who bled.

sentences.zh: 大非川之敗，薛仁貴、郭待封等不即重誅，向使早誅仁貴等，則自餘諸將豈敢失利於後哉！

translations.literal: After the defeat at Dafeichuan, Xue Rengui, Guo Daifeng, and others were not promptly punished with severity; had Rengui and the rest been punished early, would the other generals afterward have dared to fail!
translations.idiomatic: After Dafeichuan, Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng were not punished at once; had they been, which general afterward would have dared to lose?

sentences.zh: 臣恐葉蕃之平，非旦夕可冀也。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that the pacification of Yefan is not something that can be hoped for within the morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: I fear pacifying Tibet is not a victory that will come soon.

sentences.zh: 「又，出師之要，全資馬力。

translations.literal: "Moreover, the essential of dispatching armies depends entirely on horse power.
translations.idiomatic: "Again, campaigns depend entirely on horses.

sentences.zh: 臣請開畜馬之禁，使百姓皆得畜馬；

translations.literal: Your subject asks that the prohibition on raising horses be lifted, so that common people may all keep horses;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ban on private horsekeeping be lifted so the people may raise horses;

sentences.zh: 若官軍大舉，委州縣長吏以官錢增價市之，則皆為官有。

translations.literal: if the government army mounts a major campaign, entrust the prefectural and county chief officials to buy them at increased prices with official funds, and then all will become state property.
translations.idiomatic: when the army must march in force, let local officials buy them up at premium prices with state funds, and the horses become the state's.

sentences.zh: 彼胡虜恃馬力以為強，若聽人間市而畜之，乃是損彼之強為中國之利也。」

translations.literal: Those barbarians rely on horse power for their strength; if the people are allowed to buy and keep them in the markets, this is turning their strength into profit for the Middle Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians draw their strength from horses; let our people buy and keep them, and their power becomes ours.

sentences.zh: 先是禁百姓畜馬，故元忠言之。

translations.literal: Earlier the common people had been forbidden to keep horses, and so Yuanzhong spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Because commoners had been forbidden to keep horses, Yuanzhong raised the point.

sentences.zh: 上善其言，召見，令直中書省，仗內供奉。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, summoned him for audience, ordered him to serve directly at the Secretariat, and appointed him an attendant within the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, summoned him, made him a direct appointee of the Secretariat, and gave him a post in the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午，徐州刺史密貞王元曉薨。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingwu: Xu Prefecture Governor Prince Mizhen Wang Yuanxiao died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the bingwu day of the tenth month, Prince Mizhen Wang Yuanxiao, governor of Xu Prefecture, died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子，黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品來恆薨。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day renzi: Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary and Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery Lai Heng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the renzi day, Lai Heng, Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary and chancellor of the third rank, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔停來年通乾之號，以反語不善故也。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: an edict stopped the Tongqian era name for the coming year, because its reversed speech was inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict canceled the Tongqian era name for the next year, because read backward its syllables carried ill omen.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己酉，上幸東都。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day jiyou: the emperor visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the jiyou day of the first month, the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 司農卿韋弘機作宿羽、高山、上陽等宮，制度壯麗。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Wei Hongji built the Suchu, Gaoshan, Shangyang, and other palaces; their design was grand and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hongji, Minister of Revenue, built the Suchu, Gaoshan, Shangyang, and other palaces on a magnificent scale.

sentences.zh: 上陽宮臨洛水，為長廊亙一里。

translations.literal: Shangyang Palace faced the Luo River; a long gallery ran a full li.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyang Palace stood on the Luo River, with a gallery a full li in length.

sentences.zh: 宮成，上移御之。

translations.literal: When the palace was completed, the emperor moved his residence there.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace was finished, the emperor took up residence there.

sentences.zh: 侍御史狄仁傑劾奏弘機導上為奢泰，弘機坐免官。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Di Renjie impeached Hongji for leading the emperor into extravagance; Hongji was removed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Di Renjie impeached Hongji for leading the emperor into extravagance, and Hongji was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 左司郎中王本立恃恩用事，朝廷畏之。

translations.literal: Left Department Director Wang Benli relied on favor to wield power; the court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Benli of the Left Department traded on imperial favor; the court feared him.

sentences.zh: 仁傑奏其奸，請付法回，上特原之，仁傑曰：「國家雖乏英才，豈少本立輩！

translations.literal: Renjie memorialized his wickedness and asked that he be handed over to the law for trial; the emperor specially pardoned him. Renjie said: "Though the state lacks outstanding talent, is it short of men like Benli!
translations.idiomatic: Renjie exposed his crimes and asked that he be handed over for trial; the emperor pardoned him anyway. Renjie said, "The realm may lack great men, but it hardly lacks men like Benli!

sentences.zh: 陛下何惜罪人，以虧王法。

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty spare a guilty man and thereby impair royal law?
translations.idiomatic: Why spare a guilty man and wound the law itself?

sentences.zh: 必欲曲赦本立，請棄臣於無人之境，為忠貞將來之誡！」

translations.literal: If you must bend the law to pardon Benli, I ask that you cast your subject into a place where no man dwells, as a warning to the loyal and steadfast hereafter!"
translations.idiomatic: If you must pardon Benli, cast me into the wilderness as a warning to every honest man who comes after!

sentences.zh: 本立竟得罪，由是朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: In the end Benli was punished on the charge; from this the court became solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Benli was punished in the end, and the court grew sober overnight.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，右僕射、太子賓客道恭公戴至德薨。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Crown Prince Guest, Duke Daogong Dai Zhide died.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, Dai Zhide, Right Vice Director, Crown Prince Guest, and Duke Daogong, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬戌，吐蕃贊普卒，子器弩悉弄立，生八年矣。

translations.literal: Second month, day renxu: the Tibetan tsenpo died; his son Qinuixnong was enthroned—he was eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the renxu day, the Tibetan tsenpo died and his eight-year-old son Qinuixnong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 時器弩悉弄與其舅麴薩若詣羊同發兵，有弟生六年，在論欽陵軍中。

translations.literal: At that time Qinuixnong and his maternal uncle Qu Saga went to Yangtong to raise troops; he had a younger brother six years old who was in Lun Qinling's army.
translations.idiomatic: Qinuixnong was then in Yangtong with his uncle Qu Saga raising troops; a younger brother, six years old, remained with Lun Qinling's army.

sentences.zh: 國人畏欽陵之強，欲立之，欽陵不可，與薩若共立器弩悉弄。

translations.literal: The people of the state feared Qinling's strength and wished to enthrone him; Qinling would not accept it, and together with Saga they enthroned Qinuixnong.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans, fearing Qinling's power, wanted to make him king; he refused, and he and Saga together enthroned Qinuixnong.

sentences.zh: 上聞贊普卒，嗣主未定，命裴行儉乘間圖之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard the tsenpo had died and the succession was unsettled, he ordered Pei Xingjian to seize the interval and plot against them.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the tsenpo was dead and the succession unsettled, the emperor ordered Pei Xingjian to exploit the moment.

sentences.zh: 行儉曰：「欽陵為政，大臣輯睦，未可圖也。」

translations.literal: Xingjian said: "Qinling holds power; the great ministers are harmonious—this cannot yet be plotted against."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian replied, "Qinling governs and the great ministers stand together—there is nothing to exploit.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛酉，郝處俊為侍中。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinyou: Hao Chujun became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the xinyou day of the fourth month, Hao Chujun was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 偃師人明崇儼，以符咒幻術為上及天-{后}-重，官至正諫大夫。

translations.literal: Ming Chongyan of Yanshi, by talismans, incantations, and illusion arts won the esteem of the emperor and the Heavenly Empress; he rose to the office of Regular Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Chongyan of Yanshi won favor with the emperor and the Heavenly Empress through charms and conjuring, rising to Regular Adviser.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午，崇儼為盜所殺，求賊，竟不得。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day renwu: Chongyan was killed by robbers; the culprits were sought but in the end not found.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the renwu day, robbers killed Chongyan; the killers were never found.

sentences.zh: 贈崇儼侍中。

translations.literal: Chongyan was posthumously granted Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyan was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，命太子監國。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: the crown prince was ordered to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day the crown prince was put in charge of the realm.

sentences.zh: 太子處事明審，時人稱之。

translations.literal: The crown prince handled affairs with clarity and thoroughness; men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince governed with clear judgment, and contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，作紫桂宮於澠池之西。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: the Purple Cassia Palace was built west of Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day work began on the Purple Cassia Palace west of Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛亥，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day xinhai: the realm was pardoned and the era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the xinhai day, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era changed.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥十姓可汗阿史那都支及其別帥李遮匐與吐蕃連和，侵逼安西，朝議欲發兵討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ashina Duzhi, qaghan of the ten Western Turkic tribes, and his subordinate commander Li Zhefu had allied with Tibet and pressed upon Anxi; court deliberation wished to dispatch troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ashina Duzhi, qaghan of the Western Turks' ten tribes, and his lieutenant Li Zhefu had joined Tibet in threatening Anxi, and court opinion favored war.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎裴行儉曰：「吐蕃為寇，審禮覆沒，干戈未息，豈可復出師西方！

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Xingjian said: "Tibet raids as a foe; Shenli was destroyed; the weapons of war have not ceased—how can we again send armies west!
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Pei Xingjian objected: "Tibet is already at war, Shenli's army was wiped out, and the swords are not yet sheathed—how can we march west again?

sentences.zh: 今波斯王卒，其子泥洹師為質在京師，宜遣使者送歸國，道過二虜，以便宜取之，可不血刃而擒也。」

translations.literal: Now the Persian king has died; his son Nihuanshi is a hostage in the capital. It is fitting to send envoys to escort him home; passing the two barbarians, take them as opportunity allows—one can capture them without blood on the blade."
translations.idiomatic: The Persian king is dead and his son Nihuanshi is a hostage at court. Send him home with an escort, pass through the enemy camps, and seize them at the first opening—without drawing a sword.

sentences.zh: 上從之，命行儉冊立波斯王，仍為安撫大食使。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and ordered Xingjian to invest the Persian king and also made him Pacification Commissioner to the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, charged Xingjian with investing the Persian king, and made him commissioner to the Arabs.

sentences.zh: 行儉奏肅州刺史王方翼以為己副，仍令檢校安西都護。

translations.literal: Xingjian memorialized that Su Prefecture Governor Wang Fangyi serve as his deputy, and also ordered him to act as Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian asked that Wang Fangyi, governor of Su Prefecture, accompany him as deputy and act as Protector-General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己卯朔，詔以今年冬至有事於嵩山。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day jimao: an edict ordered that at this year's winter solstice rites be performed at Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, an edict announced a feng sacrifice at Mount Song on the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 初，裴行儉嘗為西州長史，及奉使過西州，吏人郊迎，行儉悉召其豪傑子弟千餘人自隨，且揚言天時方熱，未可涉遠，須稍涼乃西上。

translations.literal: Earlier, Pei Xingjian had once served as chief administrator of Xizhou; when on mission he passed through Xizhou, and officials and people met him in the suburbs. Xingjian summoned more than a thousand sons of local notables to accompany him, and publicly declared that the season was hot and one could not yet travel far—one must wait until it cooled before going west.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian had once governed Xizhou; returning on mission, he was met outside the city and took more than a thousand sons of local notables with him, announcing that the heat made a long march impossible and that he would wait for cooler weather before heading west.

sentences.zh: 阿史那都支覘知之，遂不設備。

translations.literal: Ashina Duzhi observed and learned of this, and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Duzhi heard of it and let his guard down.

sentences.zh: 行儉徐召四鎮諸胡酋長謂曰：「昔在西州，縱獵甚樂，今欲尋舊賞，誰能從吾獵者？」

translations.literal: Xingjian gradually summoned the Hu chieftains of the four garrisons and said: "In old days at Xizhou, hunting freely was great pleasure; now I wish to recover that former delight—who can follow me hunting?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian then summoned the chieftains of the four garrisons and said, "I remember fine hunts at Xizhou—who will ride with me again?

sentences.zh: 諸鬍子弟爭請從行，近得萬人。

translations.literal: Sons of the various Hu peoples vied to ask to follow; nearly ten thousand were gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Hu youths clamored to join him, and he soon had nearly ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 行儉陽為畋獵，校勒部伍，數日，遂倍道西進。

translations.literal: Xingjian pretended to hunt, drilled and ordered the ranks; after several days he then marched west by double stages.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted in name only, drilled his men for days, then raced west at forced march.

sentences.zh: 去都支部落十餘里，先遣都支所親問其安否，外示閒暇，似非討襲，續使人促召相見。

translations.literal: Ten-odd li from Duzhi's encampment, he first sent one of Duzhi's intimates to inquire after his well-being, outwardly showing leisure as if not intending a punitive strike; then he sent men to urge and summon a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li from Duzhi's camp he sent a man Duzhi trusted to inquire after his health, playing at ease as though no attack were planned, then sent again to summon him.

sentences.zh: 都支先與李遮匐約，秋中拒漢使，猝聞軍至，計無所出，帥其子弟迎謁，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Duzhi had earlier agreed with Li Zhefu to resist the Han envoy in mid-autumn; suddenly hearing the army had arrived, he had no plan, led his sons and younger kin to meet in audience, and was thereupon seized.
translations.idiomatic: Duzhi had planned with Li Zhefu to block the Chinese envoy that autumn; caught off guard by the army's arrival, he came out with his kin to greet Xingjian and was seized.

sentences.zh: 因傳其契箭，悉召諸部酋長，執送碎葉城。

translations.literal: Thereupon, passing on his tally arrows, he summoned all the chieftains of the tribes, seized them, and sent them to Suyab.
translations.idiomatic: Using Duzhi's tally arrows, he summoned every tribal chief, seized them, and sent them to Suyab.

sentences.zh: 簡其精騎，輕繼，晝夜進掩遮匐，途中，獲都支還使與遮匐使者同來；

translations.literal: Selecting elite cavalry and traveling light with minimal baggage, he pressed day and night to surprise Zhefu; on the way he captured Duzhi's returning envoy coming together with Zhefu's messenger;
translations.idiomatic: He picked elite horsemen, traveled light, and raced day and night on Zhefu; on the road he captured Duzhi's returning envoy traveling with Zhefu's messenger;

sentences.zh: 行儉釋遮匐使者，使先往諭遮匐以都支已就擒，遮匐亦降。

translations.literal: Xingjian released Zhefu's messenger and had him go ahead to inform Zhefu that Duzhi had already been captured; Zhefu also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian freed Zhefu's messenger and sent him ahead with news that Duzhi was taken; Zhefu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 於是囚都支、遮匐以歸，遣波斯王自還其國，留王方翼於安西，使築碎葉城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he imprisoned Duzhi and Zhefu and returned; he sent the Persian king back to his own state, left Wang Fangyi in Anxi, and had him build Suyab.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Duzhi and Zhefu back as prisoners, sent the Persian king home, left Wang Fangyi in Anxi, and set him to building Suyab.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，單于大都護府突厥阿史德溫傅、奉職二部俱反，立阿史那泥熟匐為可汗，二十四州酋長皆叛應之，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: at the Protectorate-General of the Pacifying North, the Turkic tribes Ashide Wenfu and Fengzhi both rebelled, enthroned Ashina Nishufu as qaghan, and chieftains of twenty-four prefectures all rebelled in response— their numbers reached several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, the Turkic tribes Ashide Wenfu and Fengzhi rebelled at the Pacifying North Protectorate, made Ashina Nishufu qaghan, and chieftains of twenty-four prefectures rose with them—several hundred thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 遣鴻臚卿單于大都護府長史蕭嗣業、右領軍衛將軍花大智、右千牛衛將軍李景嘉等將兵討之。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Xiao Siye, chief administrator of the Protectorate-General of the Pacifying North, General of the Right Valiant Guard Hua Dazhi, General of the Right Palace Guard Li Jingjia, and others were dispatched with troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Siye, chief administrator of the Pacifying North Protectorate, with Generals Hua Dazhi and Li Jingjia were sent against them.

sentences.zh: 嗣業等先戰屢捷，因不設備；

translations.literal: Siye and the rest won repeated victories in early fighting and therefore made no preparations;
translations.idiomatic: After early victories Siye and his officers grew careless;

sentences.zh: 會大雪，突厥夜襲其營，嗣業狼狽拔營走，眾遂大亂，為虜所敗，死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: It happened that heavy snow fell; the Turks raided the camp by night. Siye broke camp in disarray and fled; the host then fell into great chaos and was defeated by the foe—the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard gave cover for a night attack; Siye broke camp in panic, the army collapsed, and the dead were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 大智、景嘉引步兵且行且戰，得入單于都護府。

translations.literal: Dazhi and Jingjia led the foot soldiers, fighting as they marched, and were able to enter the Protectorate-General of the Pacifying North.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhi and Jingjia fought their infantry step by step back into the protectorate headquarters.

sentences.zh: 嗣業減死，流桂州，大智、景嘉並免官。

translations.literal: Siye's death sentence was reduced; he was banished to Guizhou. Dazhi and Jingjia were both removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Siye's death sentence was commuted to exile in Guizhou; Dazhi and Jingjia were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇定州，刺史霍王元軌命開門偃旗，虜疑有伏，懼而宵遁。

translations.literal: The Turks raided Ding Prefecture; Governor Prince Huo Yuangui ordered the gates opened and banners lowered; the foe suspected an ambush, feared, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided Ding Prefecture, Prince Huo Yuangui opened the gates and lowered the banners; the enemy suspected a trap and withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 州人李嘉運與虜通謀，事洩，上令元軌窮其黨與，元軌曰：「強寇在境，人心不安。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture, Li Jiayun, conspired with the foe; the matter leaked out. The emperor ordered Yuangui to exhaustively pursue his accomplices. Yuangui said: "A strong foe is on the border; people's hearts are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiayun of the prefecture had plotted with the enemy; when the plot leaked, the emperor ordered Yuangui to root out every accomplice. Yuangui replied, "With a strong enemy at the border, hearts are already unsteady.

sentences.zh: 若多所逮系，是驅之使叛也。」

translations.literal: If many are seized and bound, this is driving them to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Arrest too many and you drive men into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 乃獨殺嘉運，餘無所問，因自劾違制。

translations.literal: He therefore executed Jiayun alone and questioned no one else, then impeached himself for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Jiayun alone, questioned no one else, and memorialized himself for disobeying orders.

sentences.zh: 上覽表大喜，謂使者曰：「朕亦悔之，向無王，失定州矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and was greatly pleased, saying to the messenger: "I too regret it; had there been no prince, Ding Prefecture would have been lost."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with delight and told the messenger, "I too had second thoughts—without the prince, Ding Prefecture would be gone.

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷有大事，上多密敕問之。

translations.literal: From this time, whenever the court had great affairs, the emperor often sent secret edicts to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: After that, on weighty matters the emperor often sought his counsel by secret edict.

sentences.zh: 壬子，遣左金吾衛將軍曹懷舜屯井陘。

translations.literal: Day renzi: Left Golden Guard General Cao Huaishun was dispatched to encamp at Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day General Cao Huaishun of the Left Golden Guard was posted at Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 右武衛將軍崔獻屯龍門，以備突厥。

translations.literal: Right Martial Guard General Cui Xian encamped at Longmen to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: General Cui Xian of the Right Martial Guard was posted at Longmen against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 突厥扇誘奚、契丹侵掠營州，都督周道務遣戶曹始平唐休璟將兵擊破之。

translations.literal: The Turks incited and enticed the Xi and Khitan to raid and plunder Ying Prefecture; Protector Zhou Daowu dispatched Household Officer Tang Xiujing of Shiping with troops, who defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks stirred the Xi and Khitan to raid Ying Prefecture; Protector Zhou Daowu sent Tang Xiujing of Shiping against them and broke the attack.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔以突厥背誕，罷封嵩山。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: an edict, because the Turks had rebelled treacherously, canceled the feng rites at Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day an edict canceled the Mount Song rites, citing Turkish treachery.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，吐蕃文成公主遣其大臣論塞調傍來告喪，並請和親，上遣郎將宋令文詣吐蕃會贊普之葬。

translations.literal: Day guihai: Princess Wencheng of Tibet sent her great minister Lun Saitiaobang to announce mourning and also to request a marriage alliance; the emperor dispatched Commandant Song Lingwen to Tibet to attend the tsenpo's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day Princess Wencheng's minister Lun Saitiaobang came to announce the tsenpo's death and ask for a marriage alliance; the emperor sent Commandant Song Lingwen to Tibet for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊寅朔，以太子左庶子、同中書門下三品高智周為御史大夫，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day wuyin: Left Crown Prince Aide Gao Zhizhou, Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery, was made Censor-in-Chief and removed from handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day, Gao Zhizhou, Left Crown Prince Aide and chancellor, was made Censor-in-Chief and removed from the council.

sentences.zh: 癸未，上宴裴行儉，謂之曰：「卿有文武兼資，今授卿二職。」

translations.literal: Day guiwei: the emperor feasted Pei Xingjian and said to him: "You possess both civil and military qualifications; now I grant you two offices."
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day the emperor entertained Pei Xingjian and said, "You are equal to both civil and military service—I give you two posts.

sentences.zh: 乃除禮部尚書兼檢校右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Acting Great General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Rites and Acting Great General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以行儉為定襄道行軍大總管，將兵十八萬，並西軍檢校豐州都督程務挺、東軍幽州都督李文暕總三十餘萬以討突厥，並受行檢節度。

translations.literal: Day jiachen: Xingjian was made Grand Commander of the Dingxiang Circuit Army, leading one hundred eighty thousand troops; together with Cheng Wuting, Acting Governor of Feng Prefecture commanding the western army, and Li Wenyan, Governor of You Prefecture commanding the eastern army—more than three hundred thousand in all—to attack the Turks; all were placed under Xingjian's command and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day Xingjian was made grand commander on the Dingxiang circuit with one hundred eighty thousand men; Cheng Wuting on the west and Li Wenyan on the east brought the total above three hundred thousand—all under Xingjian's command.

sentences.zh: 務挺，名振之子也。

translations.literal: Wuting was the son of Mingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wuting was the son of the general Mingzhen.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，癸丑，上幸汝州之溫湯；

translations.literal: Spring, second month, day guichou: the emperor visited the hot springs of Ru Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the guichou day of the second month, the emperor visited the hot springs of Ru Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 戊午，幸嵩山處士三原田游巖所居；

translations.literal: day wuwu: he visited the dwelling of the recluse Tian Youyan of Sanyuan on Mount Song;
translations.idiomatic: on the wuwu day he visited the recluse Tian Youyan of Sanyuan on Mount Song;

sentences.zh: 己未，幸道士宗城潘師正所居，上及天-{后}-、太子皆拜之。

translations.literal: day jiwei: he visited the dwelling of the Daoist Pan Shizheng of Zongcheng; the emperor, the Heavenly Empress, and the crown prince all bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: on the jiwei day he visited the Daoist Pan Shizheng of Zongcheng, and the emperor, the Heavenly Empress, and the crown prince all bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，還東都。

translations.literal: Day yichou: he returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day he returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 三月，裴行儉大破突厥於黑山，擒其酋長奉職，可汗泥熟匐為其下所殺，以其首來降。

translations.literal: Third month: Pei Xingjian greatly defeated the Turks at Heishan, captured their chieftain Fengzhi; qaghan Nishufu was killed by his subordinates, and they sent his head to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Pei Xingjian routed the Turks at Heishan, captured Fengzhi, and received the head of Nishufu, whom his own men had killed.

sentences.zh: 初，行儉行至朔川，謂其下曰：用兵之道，撫士貴誠，制敵尚詐。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xingjian reached Shuochuan, he said to his subordinates: "In the way of using troops, cherishing sincerity in comforting soldiers is prized; in controlling the enemy, deception is honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingjian reached Shuochuan he told his officers, "War demands sincerity toward one's own men and deception toward the enemy.

sentences.zh: 前日蕭嗣業糧運為突厥所掠，士卒凍餒，故敗。

translations.literal: The other day Xiao Siye's grain convoy was plundered by the Turks; soldiers froze and starved, and therefore they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Siye lost because the Turks seized his grain train and his men froze and starved.

sentences.zh: 今突厥必復為此謀，宜有以詐之。」

translations.literal: Now the Turks will surely again use this stratagem; one ought to have some means to deceive them in turn."
translations.idiomatic: They will try the same trick again—we must answer with trickery of our own.

sentences.zh: 乃詐為糧車三百乘，每車伏壯士五人，各持陌刀、勁弩，以羸兵數百為之援，且伏精兵於險要以待之；

translations.literal: He then feigned three hundred grain carts; in each cart five stalwart men were hidden, each holding a long-handled blade and powerful crossbow, with several hundred weak soldiers as escort, and elite troops were also hidden in defiles to wait;
translations.idiomatic: He staged three hundred grain carts, each hiding five strong men with long blades and crossbows, escorted by a few hundred weak-looking troops, with elite soldiers waiting in ambush along the route;

sentences.zh: 虜果至，羸兵棄車散走。

translations.literal: The barbarians indeed arrived; the weak soldiers abandoned the carts and scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders came as expected; the decoy troops abandoned the carts and fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 虜驅車就水草，解鞍牧馬，欲取糧，壯士自車中躍出，擊之，虜驚走，復為伏兵所邀，殺獲殆盡，自是糧草運行者，虜莫敢近。

translations.literal: The barbarians drove the carts to water and grass, unslung saddles and pastured horses, and meant to take the grain; stalwart men leapt from the carts and struck them; the barbarians fled in alarm, then were intercepted by hidden troops; killed and captured were nearly all; from this time on, wherever grain and fodder were transported, the barbarians did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks drove the carts to grass and water, unsaddled to graze their horses, and moved to seize the grain—then the hidden men leapt out and attacked. They fled in panic, ran into the ambush, and were nearly wiped out. After that, raiders never dared come near a supply train.

sentences.zh: 軍至單于府北，抵暮，下營，掘塹已周，行儉遽命移就高岡；

translations.literal: The army reached north of the Chanyu Court; as evening approached they encamped; the trench had already been completed all around when Xingjian suddenly ordered a move to high ground;
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached a point north of the Chanyu Court and made camp at dusk, trenches already dug, Xingjian suddenly ordered a move to higher ground.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆言士卒已安堵，不可復動，行儉不從，趣使移。

translations.literal: All the generals said the soldiers had already settled in place and could not be moved again; Xingjian did not follow them and urgently ordered the move.
translations.idiomatic: The generals protested that the men were already settled and should not be moved again, but Xingjian refused to listen and ordered the march at once.

sentences.zh: 是夜，風雨暴至，前所營地，水深丈餘。

translations.literal: That night wind and rain burst upon them; the former campsite was more than ten feet deep in water.
translations.idiomatic: That night a violent storm broke; the campsite they had abandoned stood more than ten feet under water.

sentences.zh: 諸將驚服，問其故，行儉笑曰：「自今但從我命，不必問其所由知也。」

translations.literal: The generals were startled and convinced; they asked the reason; Xingjian smiled and said: "From now on simply follow my commands; you need not ask how I know."
translations.idiomatic: The generals were astonished and asked how he had known. Xingjian smiled and said, "From now on follow my orders and do not ask how I foresaw this."

sentences.zh: 奉職既就擒，餘黨走保狼山。

translations.literal: Fengzhi having been captured, the remaining band fled to take refuge on Mount Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fengzhi was taken, the remnant rebels fled to Mount Lang.

sentences.zh: 詔戶部尚書崔知悌馳傳詣定襄宣慰將士，且區處餘寇，行儉引軍還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Revenue Cui Zhiti to ride post-haste to Dingxiang to comfort and reassure officers and soldiers, and also to arrange matters with the remaining bandits; Xingjian led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Minister of Revenue Cui Zhiti to ride post-haste to Dingxiang to comfort the troops and deal with the remnant rebels, while Xingjian marched home.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙丑，上幸紫桂宮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day yichou: the emperor visited Zigu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the yichou day of the fourth month, the emperor visited Zigu Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，黃門侍郎聞喜、裴炎、崔知溫、中書侍郎京兆王德真並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Day wuchen: Yellow Gate Vice Director Pei Yan of Wenxi, Cui Zhiwen, and Secretariat Vice Director Wang Dezheng of Jingzhao were all made Fellows of the Secretariat-Chancellery with Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day Pei Yan of Wenxi, Cui Zhiwen, and Wang Dezheng of Jingzhao were all made chief ministers of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 知溫，知悌之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhiwen was the younger brother of Zhiti.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen was Zhiti's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吐蕃寇河源，左武衛將軍黑齒常之擊卻之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Tibet raided Heyuan; Left Martial Guard General Heichi Changzhi repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Tibet raided Heyuan; Left Martial Guard General Heichi Changzhi drove them back.

sentences.zh: 擢常之為河源軍經略大使。

translations.literal: Changzhi was promoted to Commissioner-in-Chief for the Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi was made commissioner-in-chief of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 常之以河源衝要，欲加兵戍之，而轉輸險遠，乃廣置烽戍七十餘所，開屯田五千餘頃，歲收五百餘萬石，由是戰守有備焉。

translations.literal: Changzhi, because Heyuan was strategically vital, wished to strengthen its garrison, but supply transport was perilous and distant; he therefore broadly established more than seventy beacon stations and frontier posts, opened more than five thousand qing of military colonies, and harvested more than five million shi each year—by this means both offense and defense were provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Heyuan was strategically vital, but supply lines were long and dangerous; Changzhi built more than seventy beacon stations, opened five thousand qing of military colonies, and harvested five million shi of grain a year—so the frontier could both fight and hold.

sentences.zh: 先是，劍南募兵於茂州西南築安戎城，以斷吐蕃通蠻之路。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiannan had recruited soldiers and built Fort Anyong southwest of Mao Prefecture to cut off Tibet's route to the barbarian peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier troops from Jiannan had built Fort Anyong southwest of Mao Prefecture to block Tibet's route to the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以生羌為鄉導，攻陷其城，以兵據之，由是西洱諸蠻皆降於吐蕃。

translations.literal: Tibet used the Raw Qiang as local guides, captured the fort, and occupied it with troops; thereafter the various barbarians west of Erhai all surrendered to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet used Raw Qiang guides to take the fort and hold it, and afterward the tribes west of Erhai all submitted to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃盡據羊同、党項及諸羌之地，東接涼、松、茂、巂等州；

translations.literal: Tibet fully occupied the lands of Yangtong, Tangut, and the various Qiang, bordering in the east Liang, Song, Mao, Xi, and other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Tibet now held Yangtong, Tangut, and Qiang lands, reaching east to Liang, Song, Mao, Xi, and neighboring prefectures;

sentences.zh: 南鄰天竺，西陷龜茲、疏勒等四鎮，北抵突厥，地方萬餘里，諸胡之盛，莫與為比。

translations.literal: bordering the south on India, in the west capturing the four garrisons of Kucha, Kashgar, and others, reaching the north to the Turks—its territory more than ten thousand li; among all the foreign peoples none could compare in power.
translations.idiomatic: south to India, west through the four garrisons of Kucha and Kashgar, north to the Turks—a realm of more than ten thousand li, unrivaled among the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 丙申，鄭州刺史江王元祥薨。

translations.literal: Day bingshen: Prince Jiang Yuanxiang, governor of Zheng Prefecture, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day Prince Jiang Yuanxiang, governor of Zheng Prefecture, died.

sentences.zh: 突厥餘眾圍雲州，代州都督竇懷悊、右領軍中郎將程務挺將兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Remnant Turks besieged Yun Prefecture; Governor of Dai Prefecture Dou Huaishi and Right Palace Guard Colonel Cheng Wuting led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant Turks besieged Yun Prefecture; Dou Huaishi, governor of Dai, and Cheng Wuting, a colonel of the Right Palace Guard, broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁未，上還東都。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day dingwei: the emperor returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the dingwei day, the emperor returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 中書令、檢校鄯州都督李敬玄，軍既敗，屢稱疾請還；

translations.literal: Chief Secretary and Acting Governor of Shan Prefecture Li Jingxuan, his army having been defeated, repeatedly claimed illness and asked to return;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Li Jingxuan, also acting governor of Shan Prefecture, had lost his army and repeatedly pleaded illness to come home;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 既至，無疾，詣中書視事；

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he had no illness and went to the Secretariat to attend to business;
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he showed no sign of illness and went straight to the Secretariat to work;

sentences.zh: 上怒，丁巳，貶衡州刺史。

translations.literal: the emperor was angry; on day dingsi he was demoted to governor of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; on the dingsi day he was demoted to governor of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太子賢聞宮中竊議，以賢為天-{后}-姊韓國夫人所生，內自疑懼。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xian heard private talk within the palace that Xian was born of the Heavenly Empress's elder sister, the Lady of Han, and inwardly grew fearful and doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xian heard palace whispers that he was the son of the Heavenly Empress's elder sister, the Lady of Han, and grew inwardly afraid.

sentences.zh: 明崇儼以厭勝之術為天-{后}-所信，嘗密稱「太子不堪承繼，英王貌類太宗」。

translations.literal: Ming Chongyan, trusted by the Heavenly Empress for his arts of subduing by ritual magic, once secretly declared, "The crown prince is unfit to succeed; the Prince of Ying's appearance resembles Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: Ming Chongyan, whom the Heavenly Empress trusted for his occult arts, once told her in secret, "The crown prince is unfit to succeed; the Prince of Ying looks like Taizong."

sentences.zh: 又言「相王相最貴」。

translations.literal: He also said, "The Prince of Xiang has the noblest countenance."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The Prince of Xiang has the noblest fate of all."

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-嘗命北門學士撰《少陽正范》及《孝子傳》以賜太子，又數作書誚讓之，太子愈不自安。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress had Northern Gate academicians compose Correct Standards for the Young Yang and Biographies of Filial Sons to bestow on the crown prince, and repeatedly wrote letters reproaching him; the crown prince grew ever less at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress had Northern Gate academicians write Correct Standards for the Young Yang and Biographies of Filial Sons for the crown prince, and sent letter after letter rebuking him; the prince grew ever more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 及崇儼死，賊不得，天-{后}-疑太子所為。

translations.literal: When Chongyan died and the culprit was not found, the Heavenly Empress suspected the crown prince had done it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyan was murdered and no culprit was found, the Heavenly Empress suspected the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子頗好聲色，與戶奴趙道生等狎暱，多賜之金帛。

translations.literal: The crown prince was rather fond of music and women; with the household slave Zhao Daosheng and others he was on intimate terms, and gave them much gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince indulged in music and concubines and kept intimate company with the household slave Zhao Daosheng and others, lavishing gold and silk on them.

sentences.zh: 司議郎韋承慶上書諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Wei Chengqing submitted a memorial remonstrating; the prince did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Wei Chengqing remonstrated in writing; the prince paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-使人告其事。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress sent someone to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress had the affair reported.

sentences.zh: 詔薛元超、裴炎與御史大夫高智周等雜鞫之，於東宮馬坊搜得皁甲數百領，以為反具；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xue Yuanchao, Pei Yan, and Censor-in-Chief Gao Zhizhou and others jointly to examine the case; in the Eastern Palace horse stable several hundred suits of black armor were found and taken as equipment for rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuanchao, Pei Yan, and Censor-in-Chief Gao Zhizhou were ordered to investigate; in the Eastern Palace stables they found several hundred suits of black armor as evidence of rebellion;

sentences.zh: 道生又款稱太子使道生殺崇儼。

translations.literal: Daosheng also confessed that the crown prince had ordered Daosheng to kill Chongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng also confessed that the crown prince had ordered him to kill Chongyan.

sentences.zh: 上素愛太子，遲回欲宥之，天-{后}-曰：「為人子懷逆謀，天地所不容；

translations.literal: The emperor had always loved the crown prince and hesitated, wishing to pardon him; the Heavenly Empress said: "As a son harboring treasonous designs, heaven and earth will not tolerate it;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always loved the prince and hesitated to punish him, but the Heavenly Empress said, "A son who plots treason is an offense heaven and earth cannot abide;

sentences.zh: 大義滅親，何可赦也！」

translations.literal: to destroy kinship for righteousness—how can there be pardon!"
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness demands that kin be cast aside—how can he be forgiven?

sentences.zh: 甲子，廢太子賢為庶人，遣右監門中郎將令狐智通等送賢詣京師，幽於別所，黨與皆伏誅，乃焚其甲於天津橋南以示士民。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: Crown Prince Xian was deposed as a commoner; Right Gate Guard Colonel Linghu Zhitong and others were sent to escort Xian to the capital; he was confined in a separate dwelling; all his associates were executed; then the armor was burned south of Tianjin Bridge to show officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day Prince Xian was deposed to commoner rank; Colonel Linghu Zhitong and others escorted him to the capital and held him in seclusion; his associates were executed; and the armor was burned south of Tianjin Bridge for all to see.

sentences.zh: 承慶，思謙之子也。

translations.literal: Chengqing was the son of Siqian.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing was the son of Wei Siqian.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，立左衛大將軍、雍州牧英王哲為皇太子，改元，赦天下。

translations.literal: Day yichou: Left Guard Grand General and Governor of Yong Prefecture, Prince of Ying Zhe, was established as crown prince; the era name was changed and amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day Prince of Ying Zhe, Left Guard Grand General and governor of Yong, was made crown prince; the era name was changed and a general amnesty declared.

sentences.zh: 太子洗馬劉訥言嘗撰《俳諧集》以獻賢，賢敗，搜得之，上怒曰：「以《六經》教人，猶恐不化，乃進俳諧鄙說，豈輔導之義邪！」

translations.literal: Crown Prince's Mentor Liu Neyan had once composed A Collection of Banter to present to Xian; when Xian fell, it was found in the search; the emperor angrily said: "To teach men with the Six Classics one still fears they will not be transformed—yet you present vulgar jesting talk; is this the meaning of guidance!"
translations.idiomatic: Mentor Liu Neyan had once written A Collection of Banter for Prince Xian; when Xian fell it was discovered in the search, and the emperor thundered, "The Six Classics barely suffice to teach a man—and you feed him coarse jests? Is that how a tutor serves?

sentences.zh: 流訥言於振州。

translations.literal: Neyan was exiled to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He banished Neyan to Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍高真行之子政為太子典膳丞，事與賢連，上以付其父，使自訓責。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Gao Zhenxing's son Zheng served as Director of the Crown Prince's Provision Office; the affair was linked with Xian; the emperor handed him to his father to discipline himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, son of Left Guard General Gao Zhenxing and director of the crown prince's provisions, was implicated with Xian; the emperor turned him over to his father for punishment.

sentences.zh: 政入門，真行以佩刀刺其喉，真行兄戶部侍郎審行又刺其腹，真行兄子璿斷其首，棄之道中。

translations.literal: When Zheng entered the gate, Zhenxing stabbed his throat with the sword at his belt; Zhenxing's elder brother, Vice Minister of Revenue Shenxing, stabbed his belly; Zhenxing's elder brother's son Xuan cut off his head and cast it in the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng came in, Zhenxing stabbed him in the throat with his belt sword; his brother Shenxing, vice minister of revenue, stabbed him in the belly; his nephew Xuan cut off his head and threw it into the street.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，不悅，貶真行為睦州刺史，審行為渝州刺史。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was displeased; Zhenxing was demoted to governor of Mu Prefecture, Shenxing to governor of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and demoted Zhenxing to governor of Mu Prefecture and Shenxing to governor of Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真行，士廉之子也。

translations.literal: Zhenxing was the son of Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxing was the son of Gao Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 左庶子、同中書門下三品張大安坐阿附太子，左遷普州刺史，其餘宮僚，上皆釋其罪，使復位，左庶子薛元超等皆舞蹈拜恩；

translations.literal: Left Companion and Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery Zhang Da'an, charged with favoring the crown prince, was transferred to governor of Pu Prefecture; as for the other palace staff, the emperor released them from guilt and restored their posts; Left Companion Xue Yuanchao and others all danced and bowed in gratitude;
translations.idiomatic: Left Companion Zhang Da'an, charged with favoring the deposed prince, was sent to govern Pu Prefecture; the other palace officers were pardoned and restored; Left Companion Xue Yuanchao and the rest danced and bowed in gratitude;

sentences.zh: 右庶子李義琰獨引咎涕泣，時論美之。

translations.literal: Right Companion Li Yiyan alone took blame upon himself and wept; contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Right Companion Li Yiyan alone wept and blamed himself; public opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲申，以中書侍郎、同中書門下三品王德真為相王府長史，罷政事。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jiashen: Secretariat Vice Director and Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery Wang Dezheng was made Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household and removed from active government.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the jiashen day, Wang Dezheng was made chief administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household and removed from the council.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬寅，蘇州刺史曹王明、沂州刺史嗣蔣王煒，皆坐故太子賢之黨，明降封零陵郡王，黔州安置；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day renyin: Cao Wang Ming, governor of Su Prefecture, and Li Wei, successor Prince of Jiang and governor of Yi Prefecture, were both charged as partisans of the former crown prince Xian; Ming was reduced in rank to Prince of Lingling Commandery and settled in Qian Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the renyin day, Cao Wang Ming, governor of Su, and Li Wei, Prince of Jiang and governor of Yi, were punished as associates of the deposed prince; Ming was reduced to Prince of Lingling and sent to Qian Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 煒除名，道州安置。

translations.literal: Wei was stripped of his name and settled in Dao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was stripped of his rank and sent to Dao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丙午，文成公主薨於吐蕃。

translations.literal: Day bingwu: Princess Wencheng died in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day Princess Wencheng died in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 己酉，車駕西還。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: the imperial carriage returned west.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day the emperor turned westward for the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day renshen: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month, renshen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，突厥寇原、慶等州。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: the Turks raided Yuan, Qing, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, the Turks raided Yuan, Qing, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，遣右衛將軍李知十等將兵屯涇、慶二州以備突厥。

translations.literal: Day yihai: Right Guard General Li Zhishi and others were dispatched to lead troops garrisoned at Jing and Qing prefectures to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day Li Zhishi and other generals of the Right Guard were sent to garrison Jing and Qing against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以初立太子，敕宴百官及命婦於宣政殿，引九部伎及散樂自宣政門入。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: because the crown prince had just been installed, an edict ordered a banquet for all officials and titled ladies in the Hall of Propagating Government, and the nine sections of music and miscellaneous performers were led in through the Xuanzheng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day, to celebrate the new crown prince, the court banqueted officials and titled ladies in the Hall of Propagating Government and brought the nine-section orchestra and miscellaneous performers in through the Xuanzheng Gate.

sentences.zh: 太常博士袁利貞上疏，以為：「正寢非命婦宴會之地，路門非倡優進御之所，請命婦會於別殿，九部伎自東西門入，其散樂伏望停省。」

translations.literal: Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yuan Lizhen submitted a memorial, holding that: "The main chamber is not a place for titled ladies to feast; the Gate of the Road is not a place for singers and actors to enter in service to the throne; I ask that titled ladies meet in a separate hall, the nine sections enter through the east and west gates, and the miscellaneous performers be respectfully omitted."
translations.idiomatic: Court doctor Yuan Lizhen memorialized that the main chamber was no place for titled ladies to feast, nor the Gate of the Road for entertainers to enter; he asked that the ladies meet elsewhere, the orchestra enter by the side gates, and the miscellaneous players be left out.

sentences.zh: 上乃更命置宴於麟德殿；

translations.literal: The emperor then reordered the banquet set in the Hall of Linde;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then moved the banquet to the Hall of Linde;

sentences.zh: 宴日，賜利貞帛百段。

translations.literal: on the day of the banquet he bestowed on Lizhen one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the feast he rewarded Lizhen with one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 利貞，昂之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Lizhen was the great-grandson of Angzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen was the great-grandson of Yuan Angzhi.

sentences.zh: 利貞族孫誼為蘇州刺史，自以其先自宋太尉淑以來，盡忠帝室，謂琅邪王氏雖奕世台鼎，而為歷代佐命，恥與為比，嘗曰：「所貴於名家者，為其世篤忠貞，才行相繼故也。

translations.literal: Lizhen's clansman and grandson Yi served as governor of Su Prefecture; he considered that since Song Grand Commandant Shu his ancestors had been wholly loyal to the imperial house, and though the Langye Wang clan had held the highest posts for generations, they had served as assistants in successive dynasties—he was ashamed to be compared with them, and once said: "What is prized in a great house is that generation after generation it is steeped in loyalty and integrity, and talent and conduct succeed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen's clansman Yi, governor of Su, held that since the Song Grand Commandant Shu his family had served the throne with unbroken loyalty; though the Langye Wangs had held highest office for generations, they had been assistants to every new dynasty—he scorned the comparison and said, "A great house is honored because loyalty and talent pass from father to son.

sentences.zh: 彼鬻婚姻求祿利者，又烏足貴乎！」

translations.literal: Those who sell marriage alliances to seek salary and profit—how can they be worth honoring!"
translations.idiomatic: Families that sell their daughters for office and profit—what is there to honor in that?

sentences.zh: 時人是其言。

translations.literal: Men of the time approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion sided with him.

sentences.zh: 裴行儉軍既還，突厥阿史那伏念復自立為可汗，與阿史德溫傅連兵為寇。

translations.literal: After Pei Xingjian's army had returned, the Turk Ashina Funian again established himself as qaghan and joined forces with Ashide Wenfu to raid.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingjian marched home, the Turk Ashina Funian proclaimed himself qaghan again and joined Ashide Wenfu in raiding.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以行儉為定襄道大總管，以右武衛將軍曹懷舜、幽州都督李文暕為副，將兵討之。

translations.literal: Day guisi: Xingjian was made Grand Commander of the Dingxiang Circuit; Right Martial Guard General Cao Huaishun and Governor of You Prefecture Li Wenyan were made his deputies, and they led troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day Xingjian was made grand commander on the Dingxiang circuit, with Cao Huaishun and Governor Li Wenyan as deputies, to march against them.

sentences.zh: 二月，天-{后}-表請赦杞王上金、鄱陽王素節之罪；

translations.literal: Second month: the Heavenly Empress submitted a memorial asking pardon for the crimes of Prince of Qi Shangjin and Prince of Poyang Sunjie;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Heavenly Empress asked that Prince of Qi Shangjin and Prince of Poyang Sunjie be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 以上金為沔州刺史，素節為岳州刺史，仍不聽朝集。

translations.literal: Shangjin was made governor of Mian Prefecture, Sunjie governor of Yue Prefecture, but still not permitted to attend court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjin was made governor of Mian and Sunjie governor of Yue, but neither was allowed to attend court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛卯，以劉仁軌兼太子少傅，餘如故。

translations.literal: Third month, day xinmao: Liu Ren'gui was additionally made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the xinmao day, Liu Ren'gui was additionally made junior tutor to the crown prince; his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以侍中郝處俊為太子少保，罷政事。

translations.literal: Chief Secretary Hao Chujun was made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and removed from active government.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Hao Chujun was made junior mentor to the crown prince and left the council.

sentences.zh: 少府監裴匪舒，善營利，奏賣苑中馬糞，歲得錢二十萬緡。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Workshop Pei Feishu, skilled at seeking profit, memorialized to sell horse dung from the park; each year more than two hundred thousand strings of cash would be gained.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Workshop Director Pei Feishu, a man skilled at turning profit, proposed selling horse dung from the imperial park for two hundred thousand strings of cash a year.

sentences.zh: 上以問劉仁軌，對曰：「利則厚矣，恐後代稱唐家賣馬糞，非嘉名也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Liu Ren'gui; he replied: "The profit would be great, but I fear later ages will say the house of Tang sold horse dung—not a fine name."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Liu Ren'gui, who answered, "The profit is handsome, but posterity may remember the Tang as a dynasty that sold horse dung—and that is no honorable name.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: It was therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 匪舒又為上造鏡殿，成，上與仁軌觀之，仁軌驚趨下殿。

translations.literal: Feishu also built for the emperor a Hall of Mirrors; when it was finished the emperor viewed it with Ren'gui; Ren'gui startled and hurried down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Feishu also built a Hall of Mirrors for the emperor; when it was finished Ren'gui started back and fled down the steps.

sentences.zh: 上問其故，對曰：「天無二日，土無二王，適視四壁有數天子，不祥孰甚焉！」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings—in just now looking at the four walls there were several Son of Heaven images; what omen could be more ill!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; Ren'gui said, "Heaven has but one sun, earth but one king—and I saw several emperors in those mirrored walls. What omen could be worse?

sentences.zh: 上遽令剔去。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered them scraped away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the mirrors removed at once.

sentences.zh: 曹懷舜與裨將竇義昭將前軍擊突厥。

translations.literal: Cao Huaishun and lieutenant general Dou Yizhao led the vanguard to attack the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Huaishun and Lieutenant General Dou Yizhao led the vanguard against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 或告「阿史那伏念與阿史德溫傅在黑沙北，左右才二十騎以下，可徑往取也。」

translations.literal: Someone reported, "Ashina Funian and Ashide Wenfu are north of Heisha; their attendants are barely twenty horsemen or fewer—you can go straight and capture them."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Funian and Wenfu were north of Heisha with barely twenty horsemen—a direct strike could take them.

sentences.zh: 懷舜等信之，留老弱於瓠蘆泊，帥輕銳倍道進，至黑沙，無所見，人馬疲頓，乃引兵還。

translations.literal: Huaishun and the others believed it; they left the old and weak at Hulu Lake, led picked troops by forced marches forward, reached Heisha, found nothing, men and horses exhausted—then led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishun believed it, left the weak at Hulu Lake, and marched light troops at forced pace to Heisha; finding nothing, they turned back exhausted.

sentences.zh: 會薛延陀部落欲西詣伏念，遇懷舜軍，因請降。

translations.literal: It happened that a Xueyantuo tribe wished to go west to join Funian; meeting Huaishun's army, they therefore asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: A Xueyantuo band marching west to join Funian met Huaishun's army and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 懷舜等引兵徐還，至長城北，遇溫傅，小戰，各引去。
