translations.literal: Huaishun and the others led the army slowly back; at the north of the Long Wall they met Wenfu; a small battle was fought and each side withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the slow march home they met Wenfu north of the Great Wall, fought briefly, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 至橫水，遇伏念，懷舜、義昭與李文暕及裨將劉敬同四軍合為方陳，且戰且行；

translations.literal: At Hengshui they met Funian; Huaishun, Yizhao, Li Wenyan, and Lieutenant General Liu Jingtong—the four armies combined into a square formation, fighting as they marched;
translations.idiomatic: At Hengshui they met Funian; Huaishun, Yizhao, Li Wenyan, and Liu Jingtong combined four armies in a square and fought as they marched;

sentences.zh: 經一日，伏念乘便風擊之，軍中擾亂，懷舜等棄軍走，軍遂大敗，死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: After one day Funian used a favorable wind to strike them; the army fell into disorder; Huaishun and the others abandoned the army and fled; the army was thereby greatly defeated; the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: After a day Funian attacked on a favorable wind; the army broke; Huaishun and the others fled; the defeat was catastrophic.

sentences.zh: 懷舜等收散卒，斂金帛以賂伏念，與之約和，殺牛為盟。

translations.literal: Huaishun and the others gathered scattered soldiers, collected gold and silk to bribe Funian, made a peace agreement with him, and killed an ox as covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishun gathered the survivors, paid Funian with gold and silk, made peace, and sealed it with the slaughter of an ox.

sentences.zh: 伏念北去，懷舜等乃得還。

translations.literal: Funian went north; Huaishun and the others only then were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Funian withdrew north and Huaishun's men at last got home.

sentences.zh: 夏。

translations.literal: Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Summer.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙戌，懷舜免死，流嶺南。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day bingxu: Huaishun was spared death and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the bingxu day, Huaishun was spared death and banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 己丑，河源道經略大使黑齒常之將兵擊吐蕃論贊婆於良非川，破之，收其糧畜而還。

translations.literal: Day jichou: Commissioner-in-Chief of the Heyuan Circuit Heichi Changzhi led troops to attack the Tibetan Lun Zhanpo at Liangfei River, defeated him, and collected his grain and livestock before returning.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day Changzhi defeated the Tibetan Lun Zhanpo at Liangfei River and returned with captured grain and livestock.

sentences.zh: 常之在軍七年，吐蕃深畏之，不敢犯邊。

translations.literal: Changzhi was in the army seven years; Tibet deeply feared him and did not dare violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years on the frontier Changzhi kept Tibet in awe, and they dared not raid the border.

sentences.zh: 初，太原王妃之薨也，天-{后}-請以太平公主為女官以追福。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Princess of Taiyuan died, the Heavenly Empress asked that Princess Taiping become a Daoist nun to gain merit for her soul.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess of Taiyuan died, the Heavenly Empress asked that Princess Taiping take the veil to pray for her soul.

sentences.zh: 及吐蕃求和親，請尚太平公主，上乃為之立太平觀，以公主為觀主以拒之。

translations.literal: When Tibet sought a marriage alliance and asked that Princess Taiping be given in marriage, the emperor therefore built for her the Taiping Abbey and made the princess its abbess to refuse them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet asked for a marriage alliance and sought Princess Taiping, the emperor built the Taiping Abbey and made her its abbess to refuse them.

sentences.zh: 至是，始選光祿卿汾陰薛曜之子紹尚焉。

translations.literal: At this time a match was finally chosen: Shao, son of Director of Imperial Entertainments Xue Yao of Fenyin, was given to her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Now at last Xue Shao, son of Director of Imperial Entertainments Xue Yao of Fenyin, was chosen to marry her.

sentences.zh: 紹母，太宗女城陽公主也。

translations.literal: Shao's mother was Princess Chengyang, daughter of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's mother was Princess Chengyang, Taizong's daughter.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，公主適薛氏，自興安門南至宣陽坊西。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the princess married into the Xue clan; the procession ran from south of Xing'an Gate to west of Xuanyang Ward.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the princess married into the Xue family; the procession ran from Xing'an Gate south to west of Xuanyang Ward.

sentences.zh: 燎炬相屬，夾路槐木多死。

translations.literal: Beacon torches followed one after another; many locust trees along the road died.
translations.idiomatic: Torches lined the route end to end, and many locust trees along the road were scorched to death.

sentences.zh: 紹史顗以公主寵盛，深憂之，以問族祖戶部郎中克構，克構曰：「帝甥尚主，國家故事，苟以恭慎行之，亦何傷！

translations.literal: Shao's uncle Yan, because the princess's favor was overwhelming, was deeply troubled and asked his clansman-by-descent, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue Ke Gou; Ke Gou said: "An emperor's nephew marrying a princess is an old state custom; if one carries it out with reverence and caution, what harm is there!
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yan, Shao's uncle, feared the princess's power and asked his kinsman Ke Gou of the Ministry of Revenue; Ke Gou said, "Marrying an imperial princess is an old court custom—conduct yourself with reverence and no harm need come of it.

sentences.zh: 然諺曰：『娶婦得公主，無事取官府。』

translations.literal: Yet a proverb says: "To marry and get a princess is to summon official trouble for no reason."
translations.idiomatic: But as the proverb runs, "Marry a princess and you invite the magistrate for no reason."

sentences.zh: 不得不為之懼也。

translations.literal: One cannot but be afraid of that.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot help but fear that.

sentences.zh: 天-{后}-以顗妻蕭氏及顗弟緒妻成氏非貴族，欲出之，曰：「我女豈可使與田舍女為妯娌邪！

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress, because Yan's wife was of the Xiao clan and Yan's younger brother Xu's wife was of the Cheng clan—not noble families—wished to divorce them, saying: "How can my daughter be made sister-in-law to some farm girl!
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress, because Yan's wife was a Xiao and his brother Xu's wife a Cheng—clans she deemed common—wanted them divorced, saying, "Shall my daughter call some farmer's daughter sister-in-law?

sentences.zh: 或曰：「蕭氏，瑀之侄孫，國家舊姻。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "The Xiao family are grand-nephews of Yu, an old marriage connection of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected, "Lady Xiao is a grand-niece of Xiao Yu—the court's old marriage kin."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon she stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress relented.

sentences.zh: 夏州群牧使安元壽奏：「自調露元年九月以來，喪馬一十八萬餘匹，監牧吏卒為虜所殺掠者八百餘人。」

translations.literal: An Yuanshou, Commissioner of the Xiazhou Pasturelands, memorialized: "Since the ninth month of the first year of Tiaolu, more than one hundred eighty thousand horses have been lost, and over eight hundred pasture officials and soldiers have been killed and plundered by the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: An Yuanshou, commissioner of the Xiazhou pasturelands, reported that since the ninth month of the first year of Tiaolu more than 180,000 horses had been lost and more than 800 pasture officials and soldiers killed or captured by raiders."

sentences.zh: 薛延陀達渾等五州四萬餘帳來降。

translations.literal: More than forty thousand tents of five prefectures of the Xueyantuo Dahun and others came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty thousand households from five Xueyantuo and related prefectures submitted.

sentences.zh: 甲午，左僕射兼太子少傅、同中書門下三品劉仁軌固請解僕射；

translations.literal: Day jiawu: Liu Ren'gui, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Grand Counselor, firmly requested to be relieved of the vice directorship;
translations.idiomatic: On the thirty-first day Liu Ren'gui, Left Vice Director, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and Grand Counselor, firmly asked to resign the vice directorship;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 閏七月，丁未，裴炎為侍中，崔知溫、薛元超並守中書令。

translations.literal: Intercalary seventh month, day dingwei: Pei Yan was made Palace Attendant; Cui Zhiwen and Xue Yuanchao were both made acting Secretariat Directors.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month, on the twenty-fourth day, Pei Yan was appointed Palace Attendant, and Cui Zhiwen and Xue Yuanchao acting Secretariat Directors.

sentences.zh: 上征田游巖為太子洗馬，在東宮無所規益。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Tian Youyan as Crown Prince's Stud and had him in the Eastern Palace, but he offered no remonstrance or benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Tian Youyan to serve as the crown prince's Stud, but he offered the heir no counsel or guidance.

sentences.zh: 右衛副率蔣儼以書責之曰：「足下負巢、由之俊節，傲唐、虞之聖主，聲出區宇，名流海內。

translations.literal: Jiang Yan, Deputy Commander of the Right Guard, wrote to reprove him, saying, "You bear the lofty integrity of Chaofu and Xu You, yet disdain the sage rulers of Tang and Yu; your fame resounds within the realm and your name flows across the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan, Deputy Commander of the Right Guard, wrote to rebuke him: "You claim the lofty integrity of Chaofu and Xu You, yet disdain emperors worthy of Tang and Yu; your fame fills the realm and your name is known throughout the seas.

sentences.zh: 主上屈萬乘之重，申三顧之榮，遇子以商山之客，待子以不臣之禮，將以輔導儲貳，漸染芝蘭耳。

translations.literal: The sovereign humbled the weight of ten thousand chariots and extended the honor of three visits, treating you as a guest of Mount Shang and receiving you with rites not for a subject, intending that you guide and instruct the heir and gradually imbue him with orchid and iris fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign humbled himself and honored you with three visits, treating you as a guest of Mount Shang and receiving you with rites reserved for equals, all so you might guide the heir and steep him in virtue.

sentences.zh: 皇太子春秋鼎盛，聖道未周，僕以不才，猶參庭諍，足下受調護之寄，是可言之秋，唯唯而無一談，悠悠以卒年歲。

translations.literal: The crown prince is in the full bloom of youth and the sage way is not yet complete; I, though without talent, still join in court remonstrance—yet you, entrusted with the charge of nurturing and protecting him, at the very season when speech is fitting, say only yes-yes without a single discussion, drifting idly to the end of your years.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is young and his education incomplete; I, though unworthy, still remonstrate at court—yet you, charged with nurturing him, when speech is most needed offer only empty assent and drift idly toward old age.

sentences.zh: 向使不餐周粟，僕何敢言！

translations.literal: If you had refused to eat Zhou's grain, how would I dare speak!
translations.idiomatic: Had you refused Zhou's grain like Boyi and Shuqi, I would not dare reprove you!

sentences.zh: 祿及親矣，以何酬塞？

translations.literal: Salary has reached your kin—how will you repay and fulfill your obligation?
translations.idiomatic: You now enjoy salary that reaches your kin—how will you repay the court?

sentences.zh: 想為不達，謹書起予。」

translations.literal: I thought you did not understand and respectfully wrote to rouse you."
translations.idiomatic: Thinking you had not understood, I write respectfully to stir you to action."

sentences.zh: 游巖竟不能答。

translations.literal: Youyan in the end could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Youyan could make no answer.

sentences.zh: 庚申，上以服餌，令太子監國。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: because of taking medicines the emperor ordered the crown prince to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day, while taking elixirs, the emperor ordered the crown prince to govern in his stead.

sentences.zh: 裴行儉軍於代州之陘口，多縱反間，由是阿史那伏念與阿史德溫傅浸相猜貳。

translations.literal: Pei Xingjian's army was at Yamenkou in Dai Prefecture; he spread many counter-intelligence plots, whereby Ashina Fukian and Ashide Wenfu gradually grew mutually suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian encamped at Yamenkou in Dai Prefecture and spread disinformation until Ashina Fukian and Ashide Wenfu grew mutually suspicious.

sentences.zh: 伏念留妻子輜重於金牙山，以輕騎襲曹懷舜。

translations.literal: Fukian left his wife, children, and baggage at Golden Tooth Mountain and with light cavalry raided Cao Huaishun.
translations.idiomatic: Fukian left his family and baggage at Golden Tooth Mountain and struck Cao Huaishun with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 行儉遣裨將何迦密自通漠道，程務挺自石地道掩取之。

translations.literal: Xingjian sent Lieutenant General He Jiami by the Tongmo route and Cheng Wuting by the Shidi route to seize them by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian sent He Jiami along the Tongmo route and Cheng Wuting along the Shidi route to seize them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 伏念與曹懷舜等約和而還，比至金牙山，失其妻子輜重，士卒多疾疫，乃引兵北走保細沙，行儉又使副總管劉敬同、程務挺等將單于府兵追躡之。

translations.literal: Fukian made peace with Cao Huaishun and the others and returned; when he reached Golden Tooth Mountain he had lost his wife, children, and baggage, and many soldiers suffered plague; he then led his troops north to hold Fine Sand; Xingjian again sent Deputy Commander-in-Chief Liu Jingtong, Cheng Wuting, and others leading the Chanyu Protectorate troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Fukian made peace with Cao Huaishun and withdrew; at Golden Tooth Mountain he found his family and baggage gone and many men stricken with plague; he fled north to Fine Sand, while Xingjian sent Liu Jingtong, Cheng Wuting, and others with Chanyu Protectorate troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 伏念請執溫傅以自效，然尚猶豫，又自恃道遠，唐兵必不能至，不復設備。

translations.literal: Fukian asked to seize Wenfu to prove his merit, yet still hesitated; he also trusted that the road was distant and Tang troops surely could not arrive, and no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Fukian offered to hand over Wenfu to prove his loyalty but still hesitated, trusting that the Tang army could not reach him so far north and relaxing his guard.

sentences.zh: 敬同等軍到，伏念狼狽，不能整其眾，遂執溫傅，從間道詣行儉降。

translations.literal: When Jingtong and the others' army arrived, Fukian was in disarray and could not marshal his host; he thereupon seized Wenfu and by a bypath went to Xingjian to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingtong's force arrived, Fukian was in disarray, seized Wenfu, and came to Xingjian by a hidden path to surrender.

sentences.zh: 候騎告以塵埃漲天而至，將士皆震恐。

translations.literal: Scout riders reported that dust filling the sky was approaching; officers and soldiers were all shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported a vast dust cloud approaching; officers and men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 行儉曰：「此乃伏念執溫傅來降，非他盜也。

translations.literal: Xingjian said, "This is Fukian bringing Wenfu bound to surrender—not some other bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian said, "That is Fukian bringing Wenfu in surrender—not enemy raiders.

sentences.zh: 然受降如受敵，不可無備。」

translations.literal: Yet receiving surrender is like receiving an enemy—one cannot be without preparations."
translations.idiomatic: Yet receiving surrender is like facing an enemy—we must stay prepared."

sentences.zh: 乃命嚴備，遣單使迎前勞之。

translations.literal: He then ordered strict preparations and sent a lone envoy forward to welcome and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered full precautions and sent an envoy forward to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 少選，伏念果帥酋長縛溫傅詣軍門請罪。

translations.literal: Before long Fukian indeed led chieftains binding Wenfu to the army gate to beg punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fukian arrived with chieftains binding Wenfu before the camp gate to submit.

sentences.zh: 行儉盡平突厥餘黨，以伏念、溫傅歸京師。

translations.literal: Xingjian completely pacified the remaining Turk factions and brought Fukian and Wenfu back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian pacified the remaining Turks and brought Fukian and Wenfu to the capital.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, first day bingyin: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day of the tenth month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，裴行儉等獻定襄之俘。

translations.literal: Day renxu: Pei Xingjian and others presented captives from Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day Pei Xingjian presented the captives from Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，改元。

translations.literal: Day yichou: the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，斬阿史那伏念、阿史德溫傅等五十四人於都市。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: Ashina Fukian, Ashide Wenfu, and fifty-four others were beheaded in the market of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day Ashina Fukian, Ashide Wenfu, and fifty-four others were executed in the capital marketplace.

sentences.zh: 初，行儉許伏念以不死，故降。

translations.literal: Earlier Xingjian had promised Fukian he would not die, and therefore he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian had promised Fukian his life, which was why he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 裴炎疾行儉之功，奏言：「伏念為副將張虔勖、程務挺所逼，又回紇等自磧北南向逼之，窮窘而降耳。」

translations.literal: Pei Yan resented Xingjian's achievement and memorialized, saying, "Fukian was pressed by deputy generals Zhang Qianxu and Cheng Wuting, and the Uyghurs and others also pressed him southward from north of the desert—he surrendered only in extremity."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan, jealous of Xingjian's success, memorialized that Fukian had surrendered only because Zhang Qianxu and Cheng Wuting pressed him and the Uyghurs drove him from the north—he yielded only in desperation."

sentences.zh: 遂誅之。

translations.literal: They were thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: They were executed.

sentences.zh: 行儉歎曰：「渾、浚爭功，古今所恥。

translations.literal: Xingjian sighed and said, "Hun and Jun contending for merit is a shame in all ages.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian sighed, "Hun and Jun wrangling over credit has been despised in every age.

sentences.zh: 但恐殺降，無復來者。」

translations.literal: I only fear that killing those who surrender will mean none come again."
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that executing men who surrendered will keep others from coming in."

sentences.zh: 因稱疾不出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he claimed illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon pleaded illness and withdrew from court.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，新羅王法敏卒，遣使立其子政明。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: Silla king Fammin died; envoys were sent to establish his son Jeongmyeong.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day King Fammin of Silla died; envoys were sent to install his son Jeongmyeong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸卯，徙故太子賢於巴州。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day guimao: the former crown prince Xian was moved to Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the fourth day, the former crown prince Xian was exiled to Ba Prefecture.
